meta.note: gamescom 2026 closes Sunday, Aug 30. Booth numbers and lineups are final; see the Updates tab for what changed.

event.tickets: Online-only via the official gamescom shop — no on-site box office. Sunday, the closing day, is the last one on sale, and it is on sale in every class: day ticket €31.50 (discounted €22.50), family €69.50, evening ticket from 16:00 €10.50. Wednesday through Saturday have all been and gone, every one of them sold out on day, discounted and family tickets. The Wednesday Wildcard (€65.50), the Superfan bundles and Opening Night Live sold out long before the show. The gamescom congress day ticket for Thursday was €111.00 (€40.00 discounted) and did not include entry to gamescom itself. Day tickets include free VRS public transport in the Cologne region.
crowdTips: The show floor itself has sold out to exhibitors for the first time in gamescom's 18-edition history — 233,000 m² and 1,600+ exhibitors. Expect this to be the busiest gamescom yet.

Sunday is all that is left of the show, and it is the one day you can still simply buy a ticket for — every class is on sale. Four sold-out days are behind it, so expect a full house from doors, but Sunday is the calmest of the weekend and thins further through the afternoon.

Wednesday's Wildcard and Thursday's low-crowd morning were the quietest ways into the hottest demos, and both are behind us. Sunday morning is what is left and it is the best of the rest — be at the gate for the 09:00 doors, and expect booths to start winding down through the late afternoon.

On trade Wednesday, a trade badge doesn't open every door: several AAA booths run invited-press-only previews in the morning or skip the day entirely (Xbox 2026: booth opens Thursday; Capcom 2025: press-only until ~11:00). Check a booth's own channels before planning your Wednesday around it.

Arrive well before doors open and pick the entrance nearest your first must-play booth — big booths build 2–4 h queues within the first hour. North is shortest for halls 6–9, East for Hall 10, South for the business halls; see Entrances on the Info tab.

On a trade badge the entertainment halls open at 09:00 every day — an hour before the public on Thursday and Friday. Spend that hour on the one demo you most want to play; it is the closest thing to an empty show floor you will get.
Pick 5–10 must-play booths in advance (official gamescom app + hall plan) and hit your single most-wanted booth right at opening.

gamescom runs a free Fastlane of its own: book a slot at a participating booth, then show the QR code at that booth's fast lane entrance 10 minutes early and walk past the queue. Slots open only two hours ahead on the day itself, so re-check through the day rather than planning ahead — and it needs a Koelnmesse account on the same email as your ticket.
Some booths run slots or fast-lane wristbands of their own on top of that, handed out in the morning or through their own apps — check a booth's socials the morning you go.

A few booths take free bookings on their own websites: MOZA Racing's six sim rigs in Hall 10.1 are the clearest example. Booking costs nothing and is the difference between sitting down and watching, so check the websites of any hands-on booth you care about.

Take public transport — day tickets include free VRS travel in the Cologne region and parking at the grounds is not worth the attempt. Check your line before you set off, though: Cologne's Rhine bridge works run straight through show week.

Stadtbahn lines 1, 7 and 9 do not cross the Rhine until early September: 1 and 9 terminate at Heumarkt, 7 at Neumarkt, with replacement buses from Neumarkt to Koelnmesse taking 10–20 minutes. Lines 3 and 4 still run to the East entrance and are the dependable way in.

On the rail side, RE 1, RE 5, S 1 and S 6 are cut back between Düsseldorf and Köln-Mülheim from Aug 21, and some trains skip Köln Hauptbahnhof and Köln Messe/Deutz entirely. Check your connection the morning you travel; coming from Düsseldorf, RE 6 is the recommended way round.
Evening tickets (from 16:00) are a cheap second visit and queues shrink in the last 2–3 hours — Sunday's (€10.50) is the last one on sale.
Do gamescom epix quests — completing all chapters can earn a free Sunday ticket.

Inside Cologne, KVB lines 1, 7 and 9 can't cross the Deutzer Brücke until Sept 2 — take lines 3 or 4 via Severinsbrücke to the Koelnmesse stop instead, or walk over the Hohenzollernbrücke from the Hauptbahnhof to Deutz.

onl.note: Hosted by Geoff Keighley, the ~2 h show aired Tue Aug 25 — the VOD is on YouTube, Twitch and Steam. Every game it featured wears an ONL mark in the booth lineups here, and the Featured at ONL filter lists just those booths.

2026-08-26.hours: Business 09:00–19:00, Entertainment 09:00–19:00 on a trade badge (public Wildcard entry 13:00)
2026-08-26.note: The only public entry was the €65.50 Wildcard ticket (from 13:00), and it sold out on Aug 5 — so unless you already hold one, Wednesday is trade and media only. Trade badge caveat: some big booths reserve Wednesday (or its morning) for invited press — Xbox's booth doesn't open to visitors until Thursday, and in 2025 Capcom admitted only press until about 11:00.

2026-08-27.note: Sold out in every class, the 16:00 evening ticket included — unless you already hold a Thursday ticket or a trade badge, this day is closed. If you are in, it is the best public day of the week for hands-on play: busy, but nothing like the weekend. A trade badge opens the entertainment halls at 09:00, a full hour before the public, which is the most valuable hour of the week for demos.

2026-08-28.note: Day tickets sold out ahead of the day; only the 16:00 evening ticket was left. The business area closed for the year at 20:00. gamescom GDQ speedrun showcase started (Congress Center North), and the gamescom award winners were announced at midday.

2026-08-29.note: The busiest day of the show, and it is over — the halls closed at 20:00. Day, discounted and family tickets had gone well in advance; the 16:00 evening ticket (€13.00) was the last way in. The Hall 1 stage carried the day: PietSmiet's gamescom Cup 14:00–16:50 and the gamescom cosplay contest final 17:00–19:00, with the Equal Esports Cup at The District in Hall 8 and gamescom GDQ in the Congress Center North. The City Festival downtown runs on into the evening.

2026-08-30.note: Closing day, and the only one still on sale in every class — the most relaxed of the show, though that is relative after four sold-out days. Doors at 09:00, and booths start winding down through the late afternoon, so do your must-play stops first. Free entry is possible via completed gamescom epix quests. Last day for gamescom GDQ in the Congress Center North; the Hall 1 stage runs an anime screening 13:00–14:30, and the City Festival downtown has its final evening from 17:00.

areas.Entertainment area: The consumer show: big publisher booths, playable demos, stages, giveaways.
areas.Business area: Trade visitors, press and accredited creators only (Wed–Fri, 09:00–19:00 Wed / 09:00–20:00 Thu–Fri); closed Sat/Sun. The halls sit at the South entrance, but West is the quieter way in — see Entrances.
areas.Event Arena: Big stage shows, concerts and esports (incl. Prime League offline finals) — and the stage the gamescom cosplay contest final was run on, Saturday 17:00–19:00, rather than the Cosplay Village.
areas.Cosplay Village: The cosplay community's own space: photo booths, workshops and the Artist Area. The contest itself happened elsewhere — on-site prejudging from 11:00 on Saturday, then the final show at 17:00 in the Event Arena in Hall 1.
areas.Merchandise Area: The only area where exhibitors may sell goods — main merch shopping halls.
areas.Cards & Boards Area: Card and board game communities and vendors.
areas.Indie Area / Indie Arena Booth: ~200 indie games from 182 developers — see the Indie Arena Booth exhibitor entry.
areas.Retro & Family Area: 50 years of gaming history plus family-friendly games — RC drifting, Headis and 8BitDo's retro controllers sit in this half of the hall.
areas.Campus Area: Universities, education and industry recruiting — roughly half of Hall 10.1, plus a community and youth-work block at D020/E021. Not a demo floor.
areas.Hardware & peripherals row: Not an officially named zone, but the A–D rows of Hall 10.1 are effectively the hardware hall: MOZA's sim rigs and PXN wheels, Logitech G, Corsair, PNY, Thermaltake, ASRock, a wall of keyboard and gaming-chair brands, a hi-fi corner at A070 — and the retro cluster of Commodore, Atari and MicroProse.
areas.Signing Area: Content creator autograph and meet-and-greet sessions.
areas.gamescom epix: Free digital quest program (7 story chapters, started Aug 3) — on-site booth quests, collector cards, and free Sunday tickets for completing all chapters.
areas.gamescom GDQ: A first-time Games Done Quick speedrunning charity showcase, Aug 28–30, Konrad-Adenauer-Halle (Congress Center North).
areas.City Festival: Free open-air concerts and gaming zones in Cologne's city center (Ringe), Aug 29–30 evenings.
areas.Outdoor Area P8: The reactivated open-air area behind Hall 8, back for 2026: gamescom Beach, an Asian Garden and a Community Wall, plus the outdoor half of The District. Red Bull's booth runs an EA Sports FC 27 tournament here, CD Projekt Red's Apollo Tent shows The Witcher 3: Songs of the Past, and Maverick Games gives CLUTCH its hands-on preview. Food trucks too.

entrances.lede: Four gates — South, West, East and North — all feed the central Boulevard that runs the length of the grounds from north to south. Which one you pick decides your first half hour. Koelnmesse also steers arriving crowds between gates when a queue backs up, so signs and stewards on the day overrule any plan made in advance.
entrances.trade: The standard advice is "West is best", and it holds — but mainly for the public days. On Wednesday, the trade and media day, the crowds are not there yet and you can take whichever gate suits your route. Thursday and Friday are when West earns it: South and East are carrying the public by then, and West skips both queues without making you fight through the consumer halls. Ask a taxi for West. Whichever gate you use, the badge itself is worth more than the entrance: trade access to the entertainment halls starts at 09:00 every day, a full hour before the public on Thursday and Friday.

list.West: The quiet one, and the trade pick on public days: a few minutes from halls 2–4 and the Confex without crossing a consumer hall, and the best odds of finding a taxi. No station of its own — walk from Köln Messe/Deutz, or ask the driver for West.
list.South: The main entrance and where nearly everyone arriving by rail lands: Köln Messe/Deutz station is right outside, and the business halls 2–4 plus the Confex sit directly behind it. That is also why it is the worst queue on the grounds — it was over capacity by the trade day in 2025. Allow 20–30 minutes on foot from here to Hall 8 at the far end.
list.East: Has its own tram stop (lines 3 and 4, "Koelnmesse"), opens straight into Hall 10 and is a short walk across the plaza to the business area. No longer a secret, and it absorbs South's overflow: in 2025 it was shut at one point and arrivals were routed under the grounds to West instead.
list.North: The shortest walk to the blockbuster halls 6, 7, 8 and 9. The square in front starts filling two hours before doors. Reachable on foot from the tram or by car, not by a station of its own — and from here the business area is the whole length of the Boulevard away.

xbox.description: Xbox's biggest gamescom booth ever, celebrating 25 years of Xbox: 25 games on ~140 stations, a Fable live-demo theater, daily livestreams and an Xbox FanFest on Aug 26. Bethesda/Activision titles fold into this booth. Booth open Thu/Fri 10:00–20:00, Sat/Sun 09:00–20:00 — closed on trade Wednesday except the evening FanFest (Aug 26, 20:00–23:00).
xbox.crowdNote: Largest platform booth of the show; MW4, Gears E-Day and the Fable theater will draw 2–4 h queues.
xbox.visitAdvice: Be at Hall 7 right at the 10:00 booth opening Thu or Fri, head straight to CoD MW4 or Gears E-Day; do the Fable theater (higher throughput) midday. Avoid Saturday entirely. Trade badges: don't plan around Wednesday — the booth only opens Thursday (its Wednesday has traditionally been an invited-press preview).

games.Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4: First public 6v6 multiplayer hands-on — expected to be the single biggest queue of the show.
games.Gears of War: E-Day: First public campaign hands-on ahead of the Oct 6, 2026 release.
games.Fable: Live gameplay theater by Playground Games — not hands-on (reported release Feb 23, 2027).
games.METRO 2039: First hands-on anywhere; also at Plaion's Hall 9 booth. Won Best Visuals at the gamescom award 2026.
games.Stranger Than Heaven: Sega/RGG Studio — also at SEGA's Hall 7 booth.
games.Forza Horizon 6: Drift Attack mode demo. Won Best Xbox Game at the gamescom award 2026.
games.Alien: Isolation 2: Also at SEGA's booth — compare queues.
games.The Blood of Dawnwalker: Rebel Wolves' vampire RPG — also at Bandai Namco's booth.
games.Valor Mortis: Napoleonic soulslike from One More Level.
games.Armatus: On the official Xbox Wire booth lineup.
games.Unannounced titles (~3 slots): Xbox says 25 games but has named ~22 — the last slots stayed unnamed through ONL and through both booth broadcasts on Aug 26–27, so the published lineup is very likely all of it.

nintendo.description: Nintendo's traditional giant Hall 9 booth, all-in on Switch 2 with 16 playable stations — headlined by the first publicly playable Call of Duty on Nintendo hardware in over a decade, plus a Super Mario Area from Mario Kart World to Donkey Kong Bananza. Daily fun tournaments; checking in with a Nintendo Account earns a goodie and 100 platinum points.
nintendo.crowdNote: Historically the most-queued family destination at gamescom; the MW4-on-Switch-2 novelty, Pokémon and Splatoon add up to 2 h+ waits, worst Sat/Sun.
nintendo.visitAdvice: Thu or Fri at opening; hit MW4 or 007 First Light first. Nintendo often runs virtual queue tickets via booth/app — grab a slot early. Avoid the weekend.

games.Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4: Native Switch 2 build (Infinity Ward + Digital Legends) — not cloud streaming.
games.007 First Light: IO Interactive's Bond game, hands-on all five days.
games.Minecraft Dungeons II: Switch 2 version; also at the Xbox booth.
games.Nintendo Switch Sports Resort: First-party family title — big weekend draw.
games.Pokémon Pokopia (Expansion Pass): Expansion Pass content playable — expect huge Pokémon queues.
games.Star Fox: The series reboot, out since June 25 — playable stations and a daily tournament.
games.Mario Kart World: Super Mario Area station with daily tournaments.
games.Donkey Kong Bananza: Super Mario Area station — home of the daily 'DK Challenge'.
games.Super Mario Bros. Wonder – Nintendo Swit: Super Mario Area station with daily tournaments.
games.Super Mario Galaxy + Super Mario Galaxy: The Switch 2 double-pack, in the Super Mario Area.
games.Minecraft – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition: Third-party station alongside Minecraft Dungeons II.

playstation.description: NOT exhibiting with a consumer booth — Sony skips a PlayStation booth for the seventh year running (last appearance 2019), favoring its own State of Play streams and Tokyo Game Show. Sony's only registrations in the official directory are trade- or partner-facing: SIE Deutschland on a shared industry stand in business Hall 4.1 (trade only), Sony Pictures co-located at Capcom's Hall 9.1 booth, and 'Sony Europe' plots on the open-air site north of Hall 8. PS5 titles are still playable at third-party booths (Blood of Dawnwalker, Turok, 007 First Light and more).
playstation.visitAdvice: Don't look for PlayStation on the floor — play multi-platform PS5 titles at Xbox, Bandai Namco, SEGA and other publisher booths. A surprise ONL trailer is always possible.

google-play.description: A stand near Xbox in Hall 7.1 built around a rewards hub and a live arena for Fruit Ninja, plus multigaming stations for Dave the Diver, Subway Surfers City, eFootball, Wobbly Life and Asphalt Legends Unite. Google is also running a developer session on studio partnerships and retention on Aug 26.
google-play.crowdNote: Steady but modest traffic; queues mostly for the arena and giveaways.
google-play.visitAdvice: Easy walk-in most of the day — convenient to combine with the Xbox booth in the same hall.

games.Fruit Ninja: Live arena game — Halfbrick's mobile classic gets a competitive stage.
games.Dave the Diver: Mintrocket's hit at a multigaming demo station.
games.Subway Surfers City: Sybo's title at a multigaming demo station.
games.eFootball: Konami's mobile football sim at a multigaming demo station.
games.Wobbly Life: RubberBandGames/Curve Games title at a multigaming demo station.
games.Asphalt Legends Unite: Gameloft's racer at a multigaming demo station.

capcom.description: One of Hall 9's biggest footprints (~950 m², ~60 demo stations) with two world-first hands-ons — Dragon's Dogma 2: Dark Arisen and Mega Man: Dual Override — plus Onimusha a week before launch. Rocket Beans runs the stage program.
capcom.crowdNote: Two world-first demos plus near-launch Onimusha in the most congested hall — expect 1–3 h queues for Dark Arisen and Onimusha.
capcom.visitAdvice: Go straight to Capcom at hall opening on a weekday: Dark Arisen first (fewest stations vs demand), then Onimusha. Street Fighter 6 queues stay short all day. Trade badges on Wednesday: in 2025 the booth admitted only press until about 11:00, so plan any Wednesday visit for late morning onwards.

games.Dragon's Dogma 2: Dark Arisen: World-first public hands-on of the expansion (launches Oct 9, 2026).
games.Mega Man: Dual Override: First playable demo of the 12th mainline Mega Man.
games.Onimusha: Way of the Sword: Playable weeks before its late-September release — likely the booth's biggest draw. Won Best Gameplay and Best PlayStation Game at the gamescom award 2026.
games.Street Fighter 6: Casual play stations and community matches.

sega-atlus.description: SEGA's trademark themed booth in Hall 7: Alien: Isolation 2's European hands-on debut in a claustrophobic sci-fi set, Persona 4 Revival in a recreated Junes shopping center, and Stranger Than Heaven staged as an underground jazz club. The jury gave it Best Lineup of gamescom 2026.
sega-atlus.crowdNote: Three first-time hands-ons — long individual queues but the load spreads across a big varied lineup.
sega-atlus.visitAdvice: Prioritize Alien: Isolation 2 or Persona 4 Revival first thing in the morning (Alien is also at Xbox — check both queues). Sonic and Crazy Taxi turn over fast and suit afternoons.

games.Alien: Isolation 2: European hands-on debut of the prologue; also at the Xbox booth — compare queues. Won Best Audio at the gamescom award 2026.
games.Persona 4 Revival: First Western public hands-on, in a Junes-themed area.
games.Stranger Than Heaven: First public hands-on of RGG Studio's new game; jazz-club themed area.
games.Crazy Taxi: World Tour: Early hands-on with a brand-new city map.
games.Total War: Warhammer 40,000: Hands-on debut with three Space Marine scenarios. Won Best PC Game at the gamescom award 2026.
games.Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds: Latest build incl. the TMNT pack.

bandai-namco.description: Fully playable lineup next to Ubisoft and EA in Hall 6, headlined by the world's first open hands-on of The Blood of Dawnwalker (out Sept 3) and the first playable Ace Combat 8, plus the usual spectacular photo-op builds.
bandai-namco.crowdNote: Three first-time hands-ons including a hot RPG launching during show week — Dawnwalker queues among Hall 6's longest.
bandai-namco.visitAdvice: Hit The Blood of Dawnwalker at opening, or use the Xbox booth's stations in Hall 7 as overflow. Do Ace Combat 8 the morning after its ONL showing.

games.Dragon Ball Xenoverse 3: First playable in Europe; full release 2027.
games.The Blood of Dawnwalker: World-first open sessions days before its Sept 3 launch; also at the Xbox booth.

konami.description: Main Hall 7 booth with an immersive Silent Hill: Townfall walk-through experience (new trailer at ONL), playable Castlevania: Belmont's Curse and a Metal Gear photo spot — plus a separate Yu-Gi-Oh! TCG stand in Hall 5.2 (B021/A020).
konami.crowdNote: The Townfall experience will queue like a theme-park attraction after its ONL trailer; Castlevania concentrates the demo demand.
konami.visitAdvice: Do the Silent Hill experience in the first hour of the day or the last; on a trade badge, Wednesday is better still — before the ONL trailer turns into foot traffic. Castlevania is also playable at Xbox — use the shorter queue.

games.Silent Hill: Townfall: Interactive walk-through experience, not a demo; cast revealed at ONL Aug 25, out in September.
games.Castlevania: Belmont's Curse: Playable throughout the show; also at the Xbox booth.
Photo opportunity in front of a Metal Gear unit.
games.Yu-Gi-Oh! Trading Card Game: Hands-on with the latest products at Konami's second stand, Hall 5.2 B021/A020 in the Cards & Boards Area, with staff walking newcomers through a duel; Master Duel and Duel Links are there too.

ubisoft.description: Traditional spot at the Hall 6 entrance with a playable Rayman Legends Retold demo — 20 minutes at one of 15 two-player couch co-op stations — plus the returning Community Lounge, running all five days around Rainbow Six Siege, AC Black Flag Resynced, Assassin's Creed Shadows, Anno 117, The Division 2 and The Crew Motorfest. The ONL reveals Rainbow Six Tactics and Heroes of Might and Magic III Remake stayed on the stream — only the latter is even registered on the booth page.
ubisoft.crowdNote: One playable title plus a lounge format — moderate queues, no giant new AAA hands-on this year.
ubisoft.visitAdvice: Rayman queues are manageable before noon on weekdays. The lounge splits its programme: some slots are meet-and-greets and dev sessions you have to be there for, the rest are streamed and lose nothing if you watch later. Each day's schedule goes up on screens at the stand. Ubisoft's own summary says the lounge opens Thursday, but its published schedule lists in-person sessions on trade Wednesday too.

games.Rayman Legends Retold: Demo: opening level, a new dragon-ride sequence and a classic musical level. Won Best Nintendo Switch 2 Game at the gamescom award 2026.
games.Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced: Community Lounge showcase of the Black Flag remake.
games.Assassin's Creed Shadows: Community Lounge developer talk, not a demo station.
games.Rainbow Six Siege: Community Lounge sessions rather than a demo queue.
games.Heroes of Might and Magic III Remake: Full-3D remake of the 1999 classic on the Snowdrop engine, revealed at ONL for 2027 — now registered on Ubisoft's own booth page, but no showing announced.
games.The Crew Motorfest: Community Lounge dev talk on Friday (plus a streamed session Thursday) — not a demo station.

ea.description: Back as an exhibitor with a booth at the Hall 6 entrance next to Ubisoft. EA Sports FC 27, launching weeks after the show, is the confirmed centerpiece; STAR WARS Zero Company is registered on the booth page ahead of its mid-show launch.
ea.crowdNote: FC 27 stations traditionally draw steady but fast-moving queues; busy rather than overwhelming without a big reveal.
ea.visitAdvice: FC has many stations and short rotations — fine midday.

games.EA Sports FC 27: Confirmed for the booth; launches weeks after gamescom. Switch 2 version separately confirmed at Nintendo's booth.
games.Battlefield 6 (seasonal content): German trade press said BF6 'may play a role' — but four days of show floor have brought no sign of it, and EA's booth page still registers only FC 27 and Zero Company.
games.STAR WARS Zero Company: Registered on EA's booth page ahead of its Aug 27 mid-show launch; the confirmed hands-on stations are at Xbox's Hall 7 booth.

square-enix.description: A Final Fantasy-focused fan booth in Hall 8 with play stations, photo stops and a large merch range — a community and catalog showing, with Dragon Quest VII Reimagined the one genuinely new title.
square-enix.crowdNote: Strong brand pull but no world premieres on the show floor — steady traffic for photo ops and merch; the ONL FF7 Revelation reveal (Aug 25) may bring extra attention the next morning.
square-enix.visitAdvice: Merch sells out early in the show — buy on your first pass. Good midday stop; combine with CD Projekt Red in the same hall.

games.Dragon Quest VII Reimagined: The booth's one new title — its only likely long queue.
games.Final Fantasy VII Revelation: 'New Look' presentation at Opening Night Live (Aug 25), led by director Naoki Hamaguchi with fresh footage — an ONL segment, not a show-floor demo.

cdpr.description: CDPR's first gamescom booth since 2019: extended theater presentations of The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Songs of the Past (the third Witcher 3 expansion, due 2027), running Wed–Sun after its trailer debut at Opening Night Live. The jury named it Best Booth of gamescom 2026, and visitors voted its merch and its trailer the show's best.
cdpr.crowdNote: CDPR theaters historically generate multi-hour lines (see Cyberpunk 2077 in 2019); a new Witcher reveal right after ONL will be a hall-wide magnet.
cdpr.visitAdvice: Treat it like a timed show: queue at Hall 8 opening on your first day (Wednesday on a trade badge, otherwise Thursday), or try the final showings late Sunday. Hall 8 sits at the North entrance — enter there, not via the Boulevard.

games.The Witcher 3: Songs of the Past: Cinema-style presentation, not hands-on; premiered at ONL Aug 25; releases 2027. A free Witcher 3 remaster arrives end of September.

gryphline.description: Hypergryph's global publishing brand returns with a much bigger Arknights: Endfield presence across two Hall 8.1 stand blocks: expanded interactive installations and photo spots, plus Boss Speedrun Challenges with exclusive event rewards. Visitors voted it Best Booth of gamescom 2026 in the public poll — three room-height boss installations and wraparound LED walls.
gryphline.crowdNote: Endfield's community is huge and last year's smaller booth was packed; challenge stations are the bottleneck.
gryphline.visitAdvice: Do the speedrun challenge first thing — reward stock and queue caps bite by midday; the photo installations stay accessible all day.

games.Arknights: Endfield: Boss Speedrun Challenge stations with exclusive event rewards.

snail-games.description: The ARK publisher's Hall 8.1 stand: new ARK: Survival Ascended content alongside open-universe MMO For The Stars, medieval survival sim Bellwright and sandbox builder Honeycomb: The World Beyond — headlined by 9 Yin Sutra: Immortal, with CEO Hai Shi set to unveil a second Age of Wushu-universe AAA title at the show.
snail-games.crowdNote: ARK's community is large and a AAA reveal pulls walk-up interest, but it's a mid-size stand rather than a mega-booth.
snail-games.visitAdvice: If 9 Yin Sutra: Immortal lands a splashy reveal, the stand will busy up the next morning — otherwise ARK fans can drop in most times.

games.ARK: Survival Ascended: New content and franchise developments for the survival flagship.
games.For The Stars: Showcase per Snail's lineup release — no hands-on claim.
games.Bellwright: An early look at the next major update, celebrating 1M+ players.
games.Honeycomb: The World Beyond: Look-only at the booth — the hands-on it promises is a free PC preview demo hitting Steam Aug 31, the day after the show.
games.9 Yin Sutra: Immortal: Headlines Snail's gamescom lineup after its ChinaJoy unveil — and the CEO unveils another Age of Wushu-universe AAA at the show. No hands-on announced.

plaion.description: One of Hall 9's largest booths, centered on METRO 2039 from in-house studio 4A Games — also playable at the Xbox booth in Hall 7.
plaion.crowdNote: A single high-profile shooter concentrates demand, but dual-location availability splits the queues.
plaion.visitAdvice: Compare queues at Plaion (Hall 9) vs Xbox (Hall 7) — Xbox's 140 stations often move faster.

games.METRO 2039: Focus title; also at Xbox's Hall 7 stand. Won Best Visuals at the gamescom award 2026.

krafton.description: One of Hall 9's largest presences, spread over two stand blocks (B050/C051 and B040/C041) — and all five titles are hands-on, headlined by the world-premiere PUBG: DED.NET demo straight from its ONL reveal. Interactive missions earn themed merch.
krafton.crowdNote: A PUBG-universe world premiere in the show's most congested hall guarantees heavy traffic once the reveal lands.
krafton.visitAdvice: Go first thing Thursday, or Wednesday on a trade badge, before the PUBG premiere is fully publicized; do the merch mission circuit early, before stock runs low.

games.NO LAW: Open-world FPS from The Ascent developer Neon Giant — hands-on demo.
games.Project ZETA: Hands-on: multi-team tactical arena — squads fight to secure and return the Prism.
games.Age Twisters: Hands-on: Piccolo Studio's two-player co-op age-shifting adventure — bring a partner.
games.TARAE: The Unbound: Dark-fantasy action RPG hands-on with high-pressure boss encounters.
games.PUBG: DED.NET: World-premiere hands-on of the 1990s-set PvPvE shooter, named at ONL — closed-beta signups are open.

embark.description: Riding ARC Raiders' breakout success, the Swedish studio has a Hall 6 booth reportedly twice the size of EA's — an immersive ARC Raiders supply-scavenging experience with dev meet-and-greets and merch. THE FINALS isn't part of the showing.
embark.crowdNote: Massive active player base and a first big booth — community turnout plus any new-season reveal will pack it.
embark.visitAdvice: Community events and creator meetups spike traffic unpredictably — check Embark's socials for the stage schedule and go during downtime.

games.ARC Raiders: The whole booth: an immersive supply-scavenging experience, dev meet-and-greets and merch drops.

team17-astragon.description: A group booth at B060/C061, in a stand block shared with Focus Entertainment: Team17's creature-collector LumenTale and Silver Pines alongside astragon's simulator lineup (Bus Simulator 27, Construction Simulator Evolution, Firefighting Simulator: Ignite, Seafarer: The Ship Sim).
team17-astragon.crowdNote: Indie-scale titles at a shared booth — queues short outside peak Saturday hours.
team17-astragon.visitAdvice: An easy low-queue stop while waiting out timed queues elsewhere in Hall 6.

games.Bus Simulator 27: astragon side; launches days after the show.
games.Worms: Galactic Tactics: Revealed at ONL for 2027 — the trailer also teased a 2.5D remake of the original Worms; still nothing of it at the booth.

giants-software.description: Farming Simulator's developer-publisher with its traditional community booth (plus a business-area stand in Hall 4.2) — and everything on it is hands-on this year: the Beans & Alpacas expansion premiere, Farming Simulator 26, the Switch 2 Signature Edition and Project Motor Racing, with Bale Race competitions and PMR hotlap races on the stage.
giants-software.crowdNote: One of the most loyal German communities at the show — steady all-day traffic rather than spike queues.
giants-software.visitAdvice: Easy to combine with the surrounding Hall 6.1 AAA booths; merch tends to sell out on weekend days.

games.Farming Simulator 26: The mobile edition (out since May) is what's playable; the stage adds Bale Race competitions and giveaways.
games.Farming Simulator 25: Beans & Alpacas: Hands-on premiere — first public play of the Catuaí coffee-region map before the Oct 27 launch.
games.Project Motor Racing: Playable, with hotlap races on the booth stage.
games.Farming Simulator: Signature Edition: The Nintendo Switch 2 edition of FS25 (out since Dec 9, 2025) — playable at the stand.

focus.description: A Hall 6.1 stand at B060/C061, in a stand block shared with Team17 and astragon, plus a trade-only business-area stand (Hall 4.2, A028). Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy is playable here all show, launching mid-show on Aug 27; the booth page also registers the haulage sim Road Kings, the cozy management game BioEden and the ONL reveal Elta: Defy All Gods.
focus.crowdNote: No announced blockbuster hands-on at its own stand; Resonance demand mostly absorbed by the Xbox booth.
focus.visitAdvice: Queue for Resonance at the Xbox booth, where it's confirmed playable. Focus' own stand presents Road Kings and BioEden as well, but has not said which of the three you can put your hands on there.

games.Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy: Playable demo all show at both Focus' own stand and the Xbox booth; launches mid-show Aug 27.
games.Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 3: Announced as in development and too early for hands-on; no showing of it has surfaced at the stand across the show.
games.Road Kings: Saber's 40-ton haulage sim, on Focus' booth page — its ONL trailer set the release for March 11, 2027; no hands-on announced.
games.BioEden: Cozy ecosystem-management game, out Sept 3 on PC (consoles later) — a free Steam demo is already up; presented on the booth page with no hands-on announced.
games.Elta: Defy All Gods: Science-fantasy action-platformer from the Dreamscaper team, revealed at ONL for early 2027 — on Focus' booth page, Steam demo Oct 1; booth showing unconfirmed.

hoyoverse.description: One of the biggest Asian booths of the show (~660 m², plus a business-area stand in Hall 4.2): five titles across themed zones — a Snezhnaya-themed Genshin area, Honkai: Star Rail's Planarcadia, Zenless Zone Zero, and world-premiere hands-ons for Honkai: Nexus Anima and Petit Planet.
hoyoverse.crowdNote: Historically among the longest queues at gamescom — limited-edition merch reliably produces 1–3 h lines and capacity-controlled entry, especially Sat/Sun.
hoyoverse.visitAdvice: Go at hall opening Thu/Fri and head straight for the merch counter or the Nexus Anima demo; photo zones are easier mid-afternoon. Budget half a day for demos plus merch.

games.Genshin Impact: Snezhnaya-themed zone with railway and Statue of The Seven builds; exclusive merch.
games.Zenless Zone Zero: Dedicated exhibition area with latest content.
games.Honkai: Nexus Anima: World-premiere hands-on of the new creature-collecting strategy game.
games.Petit Planet: Cozy life-sim hands-on with world exploration.
games.Nodusfall: Dark-fantasy co-op action RPG that opened ONL — its world-premiere trailer runs at the main booth from Aug 26. No hands-on, and no date or platforms yet.

level-infinite.description: Tencent's global publishing brand, next door to HoYoverse, with a fully playable three-game lineup headlined by the world-first public hands-on of Remedy's CONTROL Resonant. Themed photo spaces, a prize wheel, dev meet-and-greets and a Hunt: Showdown cosplay showcase.
level-infinite.crowdNote: CONTROL Resonant's world-first demo two months before launch will pull 60–120 min lines; adjacency to HoYoverse makes Hall 6.1 one of the most congested areas.
level-infinite.visitAdvice: Queue for CONTROL Resonant first thing in the morning; Dune and Hunt stations move faster and are fine late afternoon.

games.CONTROL Resonant: First time playable anywhere; launches Sept 24, 2026 — the booth's biggest draw.
games.Dune: Awakening (console): First public hands-on of the console build.
games.Hunt: Showdown 1896: Playable with devs present; new in-game event preview.
games.Exterminauts: Behaviour's ONL-revealed co-op shooter is registered under publisher Level Infinite at this stand — possibly the unannounced fourth hands-on slot in its lineup; nothing confirmed.

tencent-worlds-of-play.description: Tencent Games' Hall 8.1 stand is a playable Honor of Kings universe: Honor of Kings, Arena of Valor, Honor of Kings: World and a world-first Honor of Kings: ACE hands-on, with stage matchups, cosplayers and competitions — plus a playable new Beta of cozy life sim Animula Nook in a themed corner. Rust Mobile appears with prize challenges, its gameplay tent standing at gamescom Camp in the Jugendpark. The company also runs the offsite 'Worlds of Play: The Game Art Exhibition' at the Wassermannhalle (Aug 27–29): five themed zones spanning art from 40 titles, developer talks and cosplay showcases. Tencent's other playable games are at Level Infinite in Hall 6.1.
tencent-worlds-of-play.crowdNote: Timed/curated and off the main floor — moderate queues; the real crowds gather at Level Infinite.
tencent-worlds-of-play.visitAdvice: A calmer palate-cleanser between hall sessions; check whether entry needs free time-slot registration closer to the show.

games.Worlds of Play (40-title art exhibition): Art exhibition Aug 27–29, off the main show floor.
games.Honor of Kings: Playable at the stand, with stage matchups, cosplayers and competitions.
games.Arena of Valor: Playable at the stand, with competitive activities.
games.Honor of Kings: World: The open-world spin-off, out in China since April — returns with a new playable demo at the stand.
games.Honor of Kings: ACE: Playable on PC and mobile for the first time — a world-first public hands-on.
games.Rust Mobile: Show elements and prize challenges at the stand — the playable tent is at gamescom Camp in the Jugendpark, outside the fairground.
games.Roco Kingdom: The global version was revealed at ONL, first closed beta Oct 27 — still no booth showing announced.
games.Animula Nook: Hands-on: a new Beta of the cozy miniature life sim, in a themed corner of the stand with a four-metre inflatable Wupa. 10 million pre-registrations since February.

netease.description: Two Hall 7.1 booths: A051 for Sea of Remnants, and B050 for Marvel Rivals (Season 9.5 content, Jeff the Landshark statue, photo booth) and Where Winds Meet's Hidden Mountain finale. NetEase also runs a separate trade-only stand in the business area (Hall 4.2, D050), previewing Once Human's next expansion plus one unannounced title.
netease.crowdNote: Marvel Rivals is one of the biggest live-service shooters right now; 6v6 sessions cycle slowly — 45–90 min waits at peak.
netease.visitAdvice: Marvel Rivals seats 12 per cycle, so lines move in bursts — join right after a session starts. Sea of Remnants is at a separate booth (A051) from Marvel Rivals and Where Winds Meet (B050), both in Hall 7.1 near Xbox.

games.Marvel Rivals: Multi-station 6v6 setups; Season 9.5 content at booth B050.
games.Where Winds Meet: Wuxia open-world RPG; Hidden Mountain finale content at booth B050. Won Best Mobile Game at the gamescom award 2026.
games.Sea of Remnants: Hands-on at booth A051 — Orbtopia city and archipelago demo, puppet customization, daily cosplay shows; closed beta in December.
games.Once Human next expansion + unannounced: The expansion got its name at ONL: Isles of Abyss, an ocean region arriving October. Hands-on preview stays at NetEase's business-area stand (Hall 4.2, D050) — trade & media only — and the second title is still unnamed. The ONL segment was also the console launch: Once Human is now free on PS5 and Xbox, with cross-play.
games.Ananta: Registered on NetEase's booth profile with its ONL trailer — a trailer showing, no hands-on anywhere at the show. Launches Jan 15, 2027.

pearl-abyss.description: Showcasing Crimson Desert (6M+ sales) in partnership with Samsung: 30 demo PCs on Samsung's new 6K Odyssey G8 monitors, plus stage events, giveaways and cosplay. Samsung is co-registered at the stand as its tech partner.
pearl-abyss.crowdNote: 30 stations give decent throughput, but the 6K showcase plus a hit game means steady 30–60 min lines, longer on the weekend.
pearl-abyss.visitAdvice: The 30-station setup clears queues faster than most AAA booths — late morning Thu/Fri is a good window.

games.Crimson Desert: Current release build on 30 Samsung Odyssey G8 6K/165 Hz stations.

infold.description: Publisher of Infinity Nikki and Love and Deepspace, both officially at booth 9-A054 — as activity booths, not demo floors: meet-and-greets with Nikki and Momo, activity stations with exclusive merch rewards, cosplayer interactions and reservation-only giveaway packs.
infold.crowdNote: Both games have enormous, dedicated fandoms; merch and photo-op lines at comparable booths ran 60+ min in 2025.
infold.visitAdvice: Go at hall opening for limited daily merch and event slots — activity rewards tend to run out by early afternoon on public days.

games.Infinity Nikki: Official booth events, activities and exclusive merch — no demo stations; expect activity queues rather than demo lines.
games.Love and Deepspace: Confirmed at the stand Aug 26–30 — cosplayer interactions and giveaway packs redeemed via advance reservation (account Level 60+), not a playable showing.

aerosoft.description: The Paderborn simulation specialist's stand splits into play and show: emergency, hospital, haulage, forensics and rescue sims are playable, the new reveals are display-only, and a cockpit corner puts The Bus, Fernbus Simulator, SubwaySim 2 and Microsoft Flight Simulator on real rigs. A compact stand among Hall 9.1's big booths (plus a business-area stand in Hall 4.2).
aerosoft.crowdNote: Dedicated sim niche — steady interest but rarely long lines.
aerosoft.visitAdvice: Pairs into a sim circuit with GIANTS and the Team17 × astragon stand in Hall 6.1; reveal stations are busiest right after doors.

games.Winter Resort 3: Alpine ski-resort sim sequel — shown, not playable.
games.Firefighters Code Red: Firefighting sim with cross-platform multiplayer — shown, not playable.
games.Heavy Cargo: The Truck Simulator: Playable, shown with the new Heavy-South DLC.
games.Forensics: Crime Scene Detective: Playable — with real forensic experts from the state criminal police at the stand; also shown at the GameUp! Rheinland-Pfalz stand in Hall 10.2 (D043g).
games.Seaworks: Trap Season: Crab-fishing sim — shown, not playable; also at the GameUp! Rheinland-Pfalz stand in Hall 10.2 (D043g).
games.Notruf 112 – Die Feuerwehrsimulation 3: Playable station — the German emergency-services sim, third of its line.
games.Global Rescue: Playable station — rescue sim, new to the lineup.

ggg-poe2.description: A Path of Exile 2 booth in Hall 6.1 with a demo built for the show, an 'eerie display' photo op and exclusive merchandise. GGG also runs a new content reveal on the official gamescom Twitch channel on Aug 25, 20:00 CEST, the night before the show floor opens.
ggg-poe2.crowdNote: Very large, dedicated European PC-ARPG audience and a venue-exclusive demo — long, steady lines plus merch demand.
ggg-poe2.visitAdvice: Hit it early on a weekday; ask staff whether merch has a separate line from the demo queue. Catch the Aug 25 Twitch reveal beforehand for a preview of what's playable.

games.Path of Exile 2: Special demo exclusive to gamescom, post-'Return of the Ancients' era; the 1.0 launch was set for Dec 11 at ONL Aug 25.

eclipse-glow.description: The Chinese studio behind Arthurian action game Tides of Annihilation runs a hands-on demo booth in Hall 6.1 — one of the notable new Chinese single-player entrants. Its Hall 6.1, booth B050 stand is now confirmed in the official exhibitor directory.
eclipse-glow.crowdNote: High-profile trailer buzz but a single-title booth — moderate lines, spiking after any ONL appearance.
eclipse-glow.visitAdvice: If it appears at Opening Night Live, queue early the next morning before word spreads.

games.Tides of Annihilation: Expanded event-exclusive demo, Hall 6.1, booth B050, running Aug 27–30. Won Most Epic at the gamescom award 2026.

indie-arena-booth.description: The world's biggest indie booth, spread across three stand blocks in Hall 10.2 — 2026 theme 'Democratree: games for everyone': ~200 games from 182 developers across 41 countries, with publisher pods (11 bit, Fireshine, Headup, Wired Productions) and a Nintendo section with Switch/Switch 2 stations. Audio brand beyerdynamic is this year's 'First Presenter' sponsor, kitting out 230+ developer stations with MMX 300 PRO headsets and running a vinyl soundtrack listening station.
indie-arena-booth.crowdNote: Busy but far more bearable than AAA halls; short rotating lines per station, worst Saturday afternoon.
indie-arena-booth.visitAdvice: Thu/Fri morning is ideal. Browse the lineup on indiearenabooth.de or the IAB Steam curator page beforehand and pick targets — devs are at their stations, so it's the best place to actually talk to the people making the games. Combine with the Retro & Family area in the same hall.

games.Stronghold 4: Firefly's castle-sim revival — a headline title of the booth.
games.Paralives: Highly wishlisted life sim — expect one of the longer indie lines.
games.Crowded: City-builder where crows are the units.
games.There Are No Ghosts at the Grand: Friday Sundae's haunted-hotel decorating game — its ONL trailer on Aug 25 set early access for December; playable at the booth.

korea-showcase.description: KOCCA's consumer-side stand, a few steps from the Indie Arena Booth in Hall 10.2: ten Korean studios — CanOpener, Joe Yu Studio, MAYFLY, Project Moreum, Siloegi Operation, Studio BBB, SYLOPON, Team Flask, Urban Oasis and Yeop Studio — on one 131 m² block. The trade-badge Korea Pavilion in Hall 3.2 is the same agency's other stand.
korea-showcase.crowdNote: A small collective stand where each studio has a station or two; short rotating waits at best.
korea-showcase.visitAdvice: It sits right by the hall entrance, so it is an easy first or last stop on an Indie Arena Booth trip. The developers are at their own stations, which is the point of coming.

korea-pavilion.description: The Korea Creative Content Agency's business-hall stand for 13 small and mid-size Korean studios. KOCCA also runs a consumer stand in Hall 10.2, so the two-pavilion pattern of past shows survives after all. Krafton and Pearl Abyss show their own games elsewhere on the consumer floor.
korea-pavilion.accessNote: Hall 3.2 — an open demo counter with the one-on-one publisher, investor and distributor meetings booked behind it.
offers: On-site demos of the 13 participating studios' PC, console and mobile titles
One-on-one meetings with international publishers, investors and distributors

koei-tecmo.description: A small Hall 10.2 stand, registered alongside Japanese partner Gentle Giants — the program is unannounced, and Koei Tecmo's main autumn stage is Tokyo Game Show. With Attack on Titan 3 due winter 2026, some presence for it is plausible but unconfirmed.
koei-tecmo.crowdNote: Small stand in the indie/merch hall — browsing traffic unless something playable turns up.
koei-tecmo.visitAdvice: Check on-site: a playable Attack on Titan 3 or Nioh 3 station would queue fast; otherwise a quick stop on your Indie Arena Booth round.

games.Attack on Titan 3: Winter release (Dec 10) made a showing plausible, but its playable outing is TGS in September and nothing surfaced at this stand across the show — our inference, and the show has all but answered it.

bilibili.description: Chinese video/community platform and game publisher, with a booth in the indie-focused Hall 10.1. Escape From Duckov — the extraction shooter it published to half a million Steam sales in its first week — is the one game on its gamescom booth page.
bilibili.crowdNote: Modest indie-area booth; short waits except during signing/creator events.
bilibili.visitAdvice: Easy walk-up while touring the indie hall; check the app on-site for stage or giveaway schedules.

games.Escape From Duckov: Team Soda's duck extraction shooter, playable at the stand — a gamescom award nominee (Most Entertaining), and nominees are playable in the entertainment area.

aternos.description: The free Minecraft server host (Bonn-based, one of the largest in the world) runs 'MC Party' together with the Cytooxien team: four custom-built minigames — Dragon Escape, Farming, Dungeons and Paintball — played solo or in groups via a player-card queue system. Rounds earn coins to trade at the booth for Aternos/Cytooxien merch and MGA's Miniverse 'Make It Mini Minecraft' collectibles.
aternos.crowdNote: Minecraft pulls kids and families hard — steady queues for minigame rounds, heaviest on the weekend family days.
aternos.visitAdvice: Grab a player card early and drop into rounds between hall runs — coins accumulate across the day, so split visits work well. Hall 10.1 is calmest in the morning.

games.MC Party (Minecraft minigames): Dragon Escape, Farming, Dungeons and Paintball — every round earns coins redeemable for merch and prizes.

behaviour.description: Dead by Daylight's studio takes a Hall 10.1 stand in the game's 10th-anniversary year — the presence is officially confirmed, the program still isn't. Expect anniversary content and community activities rather than a AAA-style demo floor.
behaviour.crowdNote: 60M+ players and a devoted community — steady lines if meet-and-greets or photo ops run.
behaviour.visitAdvice: Check DbD's socials during the show for timed community events; otherwise an easy drop-in between Hall 10 indie sessions.

games.Dead by Daylight: Officially confirmed for the stand in the 10th-anniversary year — program unannounced; 2025's showing was community and cosplay, not demo stations.

scs-software.description: The Euro Truck Simulator 2 / American Truck Simulator studio brings its traditional community stand — truck-seat rigs running exclusive demo builds of upcoming map expansions, the returning 4D motion simulator, team meet-and-greets and merch, plus a brand-new Thrustmaster product to test first (and a business-area stand in Hall 4.1).
scs-software.crowdNote: Limited driving rigs mean moderate rotating queues; fans linger to chat with the team.
scs-software.visitAdvice: Rigs turn over slowly — come at hall opening if you want seat time.

games.Euro Truck Simulator 2: On the rigs with an exclusive Iceland-expansion demo build; the 4D motion simulator returns.
games.American Truck Simulator: British Columbia and South Dakota expansion demo builds on the rigs.

bloober-team.description: The Silent Hill 2 remake and Cronos studio's first own gamescom stand (plus a business-area stand): the first publicly playable build of Cronos: Lazarus, next to a walk-through SAW: Genesis scare activation with live performers. Cronos art also features in Tencent's offsite Worlds of Play exhibition.
bloober-team.crowdNote: A small stand with a devoted horror crowd — short lines unless a new reveal drops at ONL.
bloober-team.visitAdvice: If Bloober shows anything at Opening Night Live, expect the stand to spike the next morning — otherwise a quick stop.

games.Cronos: The New Dawn: Registered for the booth — but the actual demo is the Lazarus expansion; no standalone New Dawn station announced.
games.Cronos: Lazarus: First publicly playable build of the Warden-focused paid expansion (out Fall 2026) — more action-oriented, with teleportation and the Gladius melee weapon.
games.SAW: Genesis: A walk-through SAW-themed scare corridor with live performers — the 3v1 game itself is hands-on for press only, in the business hall.

coffee-stain.description: The Satisfactory studio — also the publisher of Valheim and Deep Rock Galactic — takes a Hall 10.1 stand. Iron Gate's devs are on it ahead of Valheim 1.0 (Sept 9), with a new trailer premiering during the show; Satisfactory's own program is still unannounced.
coffee-stain.crowdNote: Beloved catalog but a low-key stand — browsing traffic more than queues.
coffee-stain.visitAdvice: Easy drop-in next to the other Hall 10.1 publisher stands (SCS, Bloober, Kepler).

games.Satisfactory: Still nothing announced for the stand — no demo or program confirmed by day 1.
games.Valheim: Iron Gate devs at the stand ahead of Valheim 1.0 on Sept 9, when PS5 and Switch 2 versions land — a new trailer premieres during the show; hands-on unannounced.

kepler-interactive.description: The publisher collective behind Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 brings ONTOS as its featured title: a sci-fi narrative mystery from Frictional Games (SOMA, Amnesia), set aboard the repurposed moon hotel Samsara and now due 2027. The booth is a staged activation, not a demo floor.
kepler-interactive.crowdNote: Strong word-of-mouth brand but a small Hall 10.1 stand — short lines except right after any stage or ONL showing.
kepler-interactive.visitAdvice: Pair with the Indie Arena Booth one level up; afternoons are quieter once the school groups thin out.

games.ONTOS: The booth recreates the rat-server 'Experiment' with actor scientists and thought experiments — no demo stations; a hands-on gameplay video premieres Aug 26. Now due 2027.

atari.description: Anchor of Hall 10.1's retro corner: Atari's stand sits in a cluster with the revived Commodore (C059/B050) and MicroProse (A060/B061) — expect classic and modern-retro hardware, re-releases and collector merch across all three.
atari.crowdNote: Browsing traffic and nostalgic dwell time rather than queues.
atari.visitAdvice: A good low-energy stop while sitting out peak queues elsewhere; merch lines grow on Saturday.

games.RollerCoaster Tycoon: Wonderworks: Announced in the ONL pre-show (Springloaded; Steam early access this winter at $24.99) — a booth showing is still unconfirmed.

moza-racing.description: Sim-racing and flight-sim rigs, registered under parent company Gudsen Technology: six simulator stations running the 2026 hardware line — R16 Ultra and R5 Pro wheelbases, MOZA's first motion platform, an AI motion-feedback system and an AI driving coach. Sessions are free but bookable in advance on MOZA's own gamescom page, one guest per slot, and you're asked to arrive five minutes early.
moza-racing.crowdNote: Six rigs and long individual sessions mean the walk-up queue moves slowly, even though the booth never draws platform-holder crowds.
moza-racing.visitAdvice: Book before the show — it costs nothing and is the whole difference between sitting down and watching. Note MOZA's own page offers Wednesday slots and quotes 09:00 openings: Wednesday is trade & media only, and the entertainment area opens at 13:00 that day and 10:00 on Thu/Fri, so treat their times as booth-side optimism and check the day's real hours.

games.MOZA sim racing & flight rigs: Six stations split between racing and flight sim. Book a slot on MOZA's site — walk-up seat time is whatever the no-shows leave behind.

kawasaki-corleo.description: Kawasaki Heavy Industries holds a stand in the middle of Hall 10.1 under a single registered brand: CORLEO, its four-legged rideable robot concept, which the company confirmed for commercial development this year. Kawasaki has said the CORLEO riding simulator — built from motion data and 3D models captured during development — is aimed at the games and esports industries and targeted for 2027, so expect the machine and a simulator rather than a ride on the real thing.
kawasaki-corleo.crowdNote: A rideable robot horse in a games hall is a photo magnet — expect a scrum around it rather than an orderly queue.
kawasaki-corleo.visitAdvice: Worth the detour if you're in 10.1 for the hardware row anyway. Early morning or the last hour for a clear photo; the booth program is unannounced, so don't plan a day around riding it.

rc-drift-games.description: A radio-controlled drift track in Hall 10.2's Retro & Family half, registered as a club rather than a company. No screen involved, and one of the few things on the floor small children can do properly.
rc-drift-games.crowdNote: Limited controllers and a fixed track — short rotating waits, longest on the family-heavy weekend days.
rc-drift-games.visitAdvice: Good filler while someone else queues for the Indie Arena Booth two aisles over.

headis.description: Head-only table tennis, played on a full-size table with a rubber ball — a gamescom regular and the fastest way to get properly sweaty at a games show. Registered across two Hall 10.2 stands (C050/B051 and B041/C040).
headis.crowdNote: Spectators outnumber players; the wait to actually get on a table is short.
headis.visitAdvice: Not what you want an hour before a big queue — go after you're done playing for the day.

xelerate-vr.description: A German VR stand at the back of Hall 10.1 — a walking-platform experience rather than a game booth: Unco Games' co-op puzzle adventure Weeny Wise is playable on XelerateVR's own ODT omnidirectional treadmill.
xelerate-vr.crowdNote: VR sessions run one visitor at a time, so even a short line is a slow one.
xelerate-vr.visitAdvice: Ask how long a session runs before joining the queue — that number matters more than the queue length.

games.Weeny Wise: Playable on the ODT omnidirectional treadmill — Unco Games' co-op VR puzzle adventure, on Steam Q4 2026.

gamescom-lan.description: The team behind gamescom LAN — the separate BYOC LAN and esports weekend held at Koelnmesse in March — runs an on-site area in Hall 10.1. It is registered for trading card games, organisations and agency services rather than a LAN party, and hosts the partner activations filed at E071a: TikTok, EDEKA, L'Oréal and Backforce seating. Don't come expecting to plug a tower in; the LAN itself is a different event on different dates.
gamescom-lan.crowdNote: Partner activations and card tables draw a steady trickle, not a queue.
gamescom-lan.visitAdvice: Worth a pass if you play TCGs or want the giveaway-shaped part of the show; skip it if you came for demos.

commodore.description: The revived Commodore brand takes a full stand in Hall 10.1's retro corner, registered for the Commodore 64 Ultimate — the FPGA-based, cycle-accurate C64 re-creation — with the C64C Edition announced to ship late 2026. Directly alongside Atari (B041) and MicroProse (A060/B061).
commodore.crowdNote: Small stand, heavy nostalgia pull and a machine people want to put their hands on — steady browsing rather than a managed queue.
commodore.visitAdvice: Do the whole retro corner in one pass: Commodore, Atari and MicroProse sit within a few metres of each other.

microprose.description: The revived MicroProse — the Sid Meier-era sim and strategy label, relaunched out of Australia — turns its Hall 10.1 retro-corner stand into a demo floor: 15 of its 18 games are playable, with Combat Air Patrol 2 flown from a Boeing-branded motion flight seat as the centerpiece, and the developers of six titles at the booth in person.
microprose.crowdNote: A niche audience that knows exactly why it's there; expect conversation, not queues.
microprose.visitAdvice: Seventeen registered titles on one small stand means asking staff what is running rather than reading a sign. Pair it with Commodore and Atari a few stands away.

games.Combat Air Patrol 2: Military Flight Sim: The centerpiece — an AV-8B Harrier II demo flown from a Next Level Racing Boeing military flight seat.
games.Sea Power: Naval Combat in the Missile A: Playable; Triassic devs at the booth Wed–Fri, with a Falklands expansion targeted for October.
games.Death by Scrolling: At the booth, but not on MicroProse's playable list.
games.GROUND BRANCH: At the booth, but not on MicroProse's playable list.
games.Gunship Origins: Jammin Games' co-op combat-helicopter sim — shown at the booth, not on the playable list.

embracer-freemode.description: Freemode's stand is registered under three brands — Embracer Freemode, RedOctane and Stage Tour — and the relaunched Guitar Hero team's rhythm game is hands-on all five days on custom Stage Tour arcade cabinets. Its ONL segment set the release: Dec 10, 2026, with guitar, drum and microphone pre-orders open.
embracer-freemode.crowdNote: If the instruments are out on the floor this is a booth people queue for; if it's a display stand, barely a wait. Unknown until the show.
embracer-freemode.visitAdvice: Check the stand early in the day to see whether it's playable, then come back — plastic-instrument demos build the longest queues in the afternoon.

games.Stage Tour: Hands-on all five days on custom Stage Tour arcade cabinets — a Dec 10, 2026 release and instrument pre-orders were announced at ONL.

rocketwerkz.description: Dean Hall's New Zealand studio — the DayZ creator, since then Stationeers and Icarus — takes a small Hall 10.1 stand, registered for action/adventure, simulation and strategy. Lineup unannounced.
rocketwerkz.crowdNote: A small stand with a devoted but not enormous following.
rocketwerkz.visitAdvice: Low-queue stop; go when the big halls are at their worst.

frozen-district.description: The House Flipper studio, registered at Hall 10.1 under both its own name and House Flipper 2 — and, fittingly for a cleaning-simulator developer, filed under the directory's care and cleaning product group as well as games. Its booth page also registers the robot-farming sim Farmbotic, the forgery sim Forgery Craft, the dream-painting puzzler Dreampainters and a House Flipper 2 pets expansion.
frozen-district.crowdNote: Cozy-sim fans browse rather than queue.
frozen-district.visitAdvice: Two stands from Raw Fury and three from MOZA — worth folding into one pass along the A row.

games.House Flipper 2: Playable: an exclusive Pets-DLC demo, with the devs at the stand — the DLC lands Dec 3.
games.Farmbotic: Frozen Way devs at the stand; the playable build is a Steam Early Playtest running Aug 26–Sep 7, at home.
games.Forgery Craft: Art-forgery sim registered on the same booth page; no hands-on announced.
games.Dreampainters: Stability Games' first showcase abroad — devs at the booth; the Steam playtest reopens during the show.

raw-fury.description: The Swedish indie publisher behind Kingdom, Sable, Norco and Blue Prince runs a consumer stand in Hall 10.1 alongside its business stand in Hall 2.1. The 2026 lineup is unannounced.
raw-fury.crowdNote: Indie-publisher stands draw curious traffic rather than queues.
raw-fury.visitAdvice: Good discovery stop between the bigger 10.1 stands; ask what's on the machines rather than reading the signage.

area-35.description: The Japanese studio behind the TINY METAL tactics games takes a Hall 10.1 stand — and both its games are hands-on: TINY METAL 2 and the arcade party spin-off PROJECT BLITZ.
area-35.crowdNote: Turn-based tactics is a slow-burn crowd — people sit down and stay.
area-35.visitAdvice: If a machine is free, take it; the demos run long and turnover is poor.

games.PROJECT BLITZ: Playable — a 4-player arcade party game in the TINY METAL universe, shown to gauge its future role in the series.
games.TINY METAL 2: Hands-on — the series' first naval combat; Spring 2027 on PC, with an online multiplayer playtest on Steam through Sep 13.

corsair.description: Consumer stand at the front of Hall 10.1's hardware row, with a second business stand in Hall 2.2. Registered across the whole range: keyboards, mice, headsets, displays, chairs and sim-racing wheels and pedals.
corsair.crowdNote: Try-before-you-buy stations turn over quickly; merch drops are the only thing that draws a line.
corsair.visitAdvice: Any afternoon. Worth pairing with MOZA and PXN if you're shopping for a wheel.

pny.description: Graphics cards, memory and storage. PNY has trailed slim-format GeForce RTX 50 models, DDR4 and DDR5 memory, microSD Express cards for Switch 2 and a previously unannounced console SSD for its Hall 10.1 stand.
pny.crowdNote: Component stands draw lookers, not queues.
pny.visitAdvice: Quick stop; the Switch 2 microSD Express cards are the part worth asking about in person.

thermaltake.description: One of the larger stands in Hall 10.1's hardware row — cases, cooling and modded build showcases.
thermaltake.crowdNote: Show builds pull photographers; nothing to queue for.
thermaltake.visitAdvice: Any time. Good stop if you want build ideas rather than demos.

asrock.description: Motherboards, graphics cards and monitors on a compact Hall 10.1 stand.
asrock.crowdNote: One of the quieter hardware stands.
asrock.visitAdvice: Any time; a two-minute stop unless you're shopping.

pxn.description: Budget sim-racing gear — wheels and pedal sets — a few rows from MOZA's rigs in the same hall. PXN's own announcement gave booth C029; C041 is what the official directory lists, so go by the hall plan.
pxn.visitAdvice: The cheap end of the wheel market — useful to try back-to-back with MOZA at A022 before you spend anything.

8bitdo.description: Retro-styled controllers, keyboards and adapters, sharing Clear River Games' stand in Hall 10.2 — a short walk from the Indie Arena Booth and in the same half of the hall as the Retro & Family area.
8bitdo.crowdNote: Small shared stand; browsing traffic that thickens at the weekend.
8bitdo.visitAdvice: Fold it into an Indie Arena Booth trip rather than making a separate journey.

konsolenfan-audio.description: A shared hi-fi stand that is genuinely odd for a games show: konsolenfan.de hosts Yamaha, Genelec, ELAC, Canton, clearaudio, Oehlbach and Sharp under one booth number, with LiberNovo seating alongside. Eight separate companies are registered at A070.
konsolenfan-audio.crowdNote: Almost nobody comes to gamescom for loudspeakers — one of the quietest corners of a busy hall.
konsolenfan-audio.visitAdvice: A good place to sit out someone else's queue, and about the only stand on the floor where you can hear anything properly.

daedalic.description: The Hamburg adventure-game publisher returns with a six-title Hall 10.2 booth, revealed at its first-ever "Daedalic Days" showcase on Aug 13: new adventures Woodo, Ghost Haunting and Star Trek: Voyager — Across the Unknown, alongside returning names Surviving Deponia, Horseguard: Winds of the North and The Curse of the Crimson Stag. Most titles are playable on the show floor.
daedalic.crowdNote: An adventure-game crowd rather than an AAA one — steady interest, rarely a long line.
daedalic.visitAdvice: Easy walk-up in the Hall 10.2 indie area any day of the show.

games.Woodo: New adventure title, first revealed at Daedalic Days.
games.Ghost Haunting: New adventure title, first revealed at Daedalic Days.
games.Star Trek: Voyager — Across the Unknown: New Star Trek adventure game, first shown at Daedalic Days.
games.Surviving Deponia: Returning entry in the Deponia adventure series.

indie-castle.description: A community booth built as an actual castle, four metres tall, in the indie half of Hall 10.2: 52 games on pods along the outside walls and in the courtyard, from around forty small studios and publishers. It is the first outing of the Indies United brand and is run by Hamburg's Insomnia Development; Dotemu, gamigo and Daedalic have pods here too.
indie-castle.crowdNote: Forty small pods rather than one queue — waits are per-machine and short, busiest on Saturday afternoon.
indie-castle.visitAdvice: Circle the outside walls first, then go into the courtyard — the pods inside are easy to walk past. It sits between the Indie Arena Booth and the Retro & Family Area, so it fits into the same Hall 10.2 pass.

a-maze.description: The Berlin independent-games festival's third Digital PlayGround at gamescom: experimental and art games curated well outside what the Indie Arena Booth covers, a few stands away in the same hall.
a-maze.crowdNote: Small, curated and quiet next to the Indie Arena Booth — machines free up quickly.
a-maze.visitAdvice: The best antidote to a day of AAA queues. Go when the Indie Arena Booth is at its busiest.

gamescom-campus.description: Roughly half of Hall 10.1 is not a games floor at all. The Campus area runs education and recruiting — universities, SAE, PIXL VISN and IU alongside employers from the Bundeswehr and Rheinmetall to Siemens, Airbus, DATEV and several state police forces — plus a large community and youth-work block at D020/E021: jfc Medienzentrum, Gaming Ohne Grenzen, AbleGamers, youth-protection groups and the city of Cologne. Worth knowing before you walk into 10.1 expecting demos.
gamescom-campus.crowdNote: Busy with school groups on the trade days, quiet at the weekend — never a queue.
gamescom-campus.visitAdvice: Skip it unless you're job-hunting or studying. It is, however, a genuinely calm place to sit down mid-day, and the accessibility and youth-work stands are worth a look.

lego.description: Multi-stand block in Hall 9.1 next to Nintendo, walked as a ring of themed zones. Four things are playable: the Mayhem Collection DLC for LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight, the LEGO Fortnite modes, Minecraft Dungeons II, and Forza Horizon 6 from brick-built racing rigs. The rest is display and photo ops — LEGO Skylines, Super Mario, Pokémon, One Piece — plus a shop selling sets at 20% off.
lego.crowdNote: Family magnet in the same hall as Nintendo — four demo zones and as many photo ops, and the lines get long on the weekend.
lego.visitAdvice: Weekday mornings; weekends are dominated by families. There is more hands-on here than the booth looks, and most of it rewards you: high scores at the Batman demo win a full set, the Forza rigs have prizes for beating target times, and a stamp rally passport from the shop counter redeems a gold LEGO charm once you have collected stamps across the zones.

games.LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight: Playable demo of the Mayhem Collection DLC before its Sept 18 release — the Switch 2 version lands the same day. Everyone gets the Retro Video Game Batman minifigure; a high score wins a full LEGO Batman set.
games.LEGO Fortnite: Playable: demos of the various modes, entered through a life-size recreation of the Rave Cave set, with Loot Llama and Cuddle Team Leader builds and a dance photo station.
games.LEGO Skylines: Announced at Opening Night Live and given its own zone here, but not playable — a LEGO construction-zone photo op and a prize wheel handing out stickers, bags, lanyards and small Technic sets.
games.Minecraft Dungeons II: Playable demos in the LEGO Minecraft zone, beside the physical sets and a very large Creeper build.
games.Forza Horizon 6: Played sitting in brick-built racing sim rigs in the middle of the booth, with prizes for beating the target times.

wizards-of-the-coast.description: Wizards of the Coast anchors the trading-card corner of Hall 5.2, sharing its stand block with European distributor ADC Blackfire. Expect learn-to-play tables and 2026-set demos (this year's slate includes Reality Fracture and previews of The Hobbit crossover). Konami's separate Yu-Gi-Oh! stand, Ravensburger, Pegasus and Panini fill out the same hall.
wizards-of-the-coast.crowdNote: The card-game hall gets dense on public days, and promo giveaways cause morning rushes.
wizards-of-the-coast.visitAdvice: Morning for promos, late afternoon for a relaxed learn-to-play seat.

games.Magic: The Gathering: Learn-to-play and casual play tables; promo cards usually while daily stocks last.

asus-rog.description: Large Hall 8.1 presence across B041/C040 and B040, plus an outdoor area at Hall 8 North: ROG laptops, monitors and the ROG Xbox Ally handheld family playable on-site.
asus-rog.crowdNote: ROG handheld try-out stations build 15–45 min lines; the rest flows freely.
asus-rog.visitAdvice: Morning visit if you want hands-on time with the ROG Ally handhelds.

samsung.description: Odyssey gaming monitors and SSDs in Hall 9.1, built around a hands-on demo zone: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 playable two months before its Oct 23 release, on the 2027 Odyssey line — a 49-inch 360 Hz OLED G9, a 42-inch curved OLED G7, a 4K OLED G8 and a 1,100 Hz G6. Samsung is also co-registered at Pearl Abyss's B010/C011 stand nearby, which it powers with 6K Odyssey G8 displays.
samsung.crowdNote: An early hands-on with Modern Warfare 4 in Hall 9's foot traffic makes this busier than a monitor stand would normally be, though station turnover is fast.
samsung.visitAdvice: Combine with your Nintendo Hall 9 visit — but come early in the day if Modern Warfare 4 is the point, because Samsung raffles 500 Vault Edition game codes to booth visitors.

games.Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4: Playable here as well as at Xbox, ahead of the Oct 23 release, on Odyssey monitors under Samsung's HDR10+ GAMING deal with Activision. 500 Vault Edition codes are raffled at the booth.
games.Cronos: The New Dawn: One of the titles Samsung runs on the Odyssey panels; whether you can play it here is not stated.
games.Cyberpunk 2077: A showcase title for the OLED panels; whether you can play it here is not stated.

razer.description: Two locations: the consumer stand in Hall 10.2 and a business stand in Hall 2.2. Hands-on with the 2026 peripheral line from its big CES slate, plus esports events and merch drops.
razer.crowdNote: Solid fan traffic for limited merch and giveaway drops, but nothing like platform-holder queues.
razer.visitAdvice: For limited merch, go early on the first public day; otherwise any weekday afternoon.

logitech.description: Logitech G's own stand in Hall 10.1's hardware row: gaming mice, keyboards, headsets and sim-racing rigs with try-before-you-buy stations. A separate Logitech GmbH stand shares Hall 8.1's A065 with Acer and Philips monitors, but has no gamescom profile of its own.
logitech.crowdNote: Browse-through booth; only sim-racing rigs generate short waits.
logitech.visitAdvice: Any time works; sim rigs are quietest weekday mornings.

aula.description: Mice, keyboards and other peripherals from the Chinese hardware brand, registered under its legal entity Shenzhen Suoai Electronics Technology — one of Hall 10.1's less obvious hardware-row stands.
aula.crowdNote: A quiet component stand, not a destination booth.
aula.visitAdvice: A quick look if you're already working the hardware row.

aoc-agon.description: AOC's gaming-monitor brand with its latest high-refresh OLED and Mini-LED monitors on demo stations.
aoc-agon.visitAdvice: Walk in anytime; pairs well with Logitech and ASUS in the same hall.

amd.description: AMD shares a Hall 7.1 stand block with Webedia's community area, Vodafone, ZOTAC and the Driveball Arena — expect Ryzen/Radeon rigs powering partner setups rather than a standalone AMD mega-booth. AMD also hosts its own Cologne event on Aug 23, teasing a Radeon announcement right before the show.
amd.crowdNote: Traffic on the shared block follows the community-stage program and creator meetups more than AMD itself.
amd.visitAdvice: Worth a pass if you're PC-hardware shopping; check the community area's stage schedule for creator sessions.

wargaming.description: NOT exhibiting on the show floor: Wargaming cancelled the Hall 1 Event Arena presence it had in 2025, and the official directory lists only B2B stands in trade halls 3.2 and 2.2, nothing in the entertainment area. Its one public appearance is the offsite Wargaming Community Party on Aug 28 at HERBRAND's Ehrenfeld (~€10, Eventbrite), covering WoT, WoWs, Blitz and World of Tanks: HEAT.
wargaming.crowdNote: No show-floor booth in 2026, so nothing to queue for on-site; the offsite party is ticketed and capped separately.
wargaming.visitAdvice: Skip the show floor for Wargaming — grab Community Party tickets on Eventbrite early if you're a player, since it's capped.

games.World of Tanks / Warships / HEAT: No show-floor demo booth in 2026 — only the offsite Community Party (Aug 28, HERBRAND's Ehrenfeld), a social meet-up with devs and community rather than a demo event.

kuro-games.description: Did not exhibit in 2026: no booth, and no announcement all summer — Kuro's year is WuWa's 3.6 broadcast, the Elysium anime and its concert tour. Wuthering Waves appears at the show only as artwork inside Tencent's offsite Worlds of Play exhibition.
kuro-games.crowdNote: Nothing confirmed to queue for; if a booth materializes expect HoYoverse-style merch crowds.
kuro-games.visitAdvice: Don't plan around Kuro Games; re-check the official directory and @Wuthering_Waves socials in the final two weeks.

take-two.description: No consumer booth: Take-Two's only registration in the official directory is a shared industry stand in business Hall 4.1 (trade only), and 2K sat the show out too. The GTA 6 moment happens offsite: an 'Extended Look' premieres on Netflix on Thursday Aug 27 (YouTube six hours later), deliberately timed to gamescom week. GTA 6 launches Nov 19, 2026.
take-two.visitAdvice: Watch the GTA 6 Extended Look on Netflix/YouTube on Aug 27 during the show; keep an eye on late exhibitor updates in case 2K books space.

games.Grand Theft Auto VI — Extended Look: Streaming showcase on Netflix Aug 27, 21:00 CEST — not at the show.

thq-nordic.description: NOT attending — officially cancelled its gamescom 2026 presence (July 8), citing a lack of showcase-ready titles; it hopes to return in 2027. Its Digital Showcase on Aug 7 (Titan Quest II, Wreckfest 2, Gothic Remake) replaces the physical showing.
thq-nordic.visitAdvice: Watch the THQ Nordic Digital Showcase stream instead; partner titles may still surface at other booths.

games.Titan Quest II / Wreckfest 2 / Gothic Re: Digital Showcase (streamed Aug 7) only — no gamescom booth.

invoke-archetype.description: Two Wizards of the Coast games premiere at Opening Night Live on Aug 25 and neither reaches the public floor: Invoke's Warlock: Dungeons & Dragons gets its first gameplay, Archetype's Exodus a new trailer and a companion reveal. Both studios are registered only on Hasbro's shared business stand (Hall 2.2, A014/B015) next to Wizards of the Coast LLC — trade badges only, no demo. Both games are due in 2027.
invoke-archetype.crowdNote: No consumer booth to queue for.
invoke-archetype.visitAdvice: Watch the ONL stream on Tuesday evening. On the floor, the Wizards of the Coast stand in Hall 5.2 is a Magic: The Gathering card booth and shows neither game.

games.Warlock: Dungeons & Dragons: First gameplay at ONL Aug 25 — Invoke's D&D action-adventure, out 2027. Stream only, no show-floor demo.
games.Exodus: New trailer, a companion reveal and a date at ONL: Archetype's sci-fi RPG launches April 7, 2027. Stream only, no show-floor demo.

playside.description: No consumer booth: PlaySide's only registration in the official directory is its own stand in business Hall 3.2 (C010/D011, trade only). The full gameplay reveal for Game of Thrones: War for Westeros — a premium real-time strategy game for PC — premieres at Opening Night Live on Aug 25, ahead of an early 2027 release.
playside.visitAdvice: Catch it in the ONL stream on Tuesday evening; there is nothing to plan a floor stop around.

games.Game of Thrones: War for Westeros: Gameplay reveal trailer at ONL Aug 25 — four playable factions, PC only, early 2027. Stream only, no demo at the show.

ncsoft.description: Three NC (NCSOFT) games premiered at Opening Night Live on Aug 25 and none of them reaches the public floor: AION 2 took an Oct 5 launch date, Cinder City got a story trailer, and Project Bonfire was revealed as Like or Die. NC's only stand at the show is the closed business booth in Hall 4.2, where the lineup was shown to press and industry by appointment.
ncsoft.crowdNote: No consumer booth to queue for.
ncsoft.visitAdvice: Nothing to plan a floor stop around — the three trailers are in the ONL stream from Tuesday evening, and Cinder City and Like or Die both have Steam pages if you want to follow them.

games.AION 2: Launch date at ONL Aug 25: the AION sequel goes live Oct 5 on Steam and NC's own PURPLE, with five days of head start for Founder's Pack owners from Sept 30. Stream only, no show-floor demo.
games.Cinder City: Story-and-setting trailer at ONL Aug 25 — BigFire Games' open-world cinematic third-person shooter, set in a fallen near-future Seoul and still without a release date. Shown to press and industry at NC's business booth; nothing to play on the public floor.
