games.Like or Die: World premiere at ONL Aug 25, where Project Bonfire got its name: a team-based survival FPS whose streamers reshape the map with blocks mid-match. PC via Steam, no date. Stream only, no show-floor demo.

paradox-urban.description: No booth of its own: Paradox co-presents Transport Fever 3 with Urban Games, whose stand is in Hall 8.1 at B053a — complete with a London double-decker bus as the eye-catcher. Paradox is separately registered at Level Infinite's shared Hall 6.1 stand, with nothing announced there.
paradox-urban.crowdNote: Niche-but-devoted audience — steady sim fans rather than mass queues.
paradox-urban.visitAdvice: Queues reasonable even at peak; combine with CDPR and Square Enix in the same hall.

games.Transport Fever 3: Hands-on sessions of up to an hour at the demo stations, bookable via gamescom fastlane — and the show brought a release date: Sept 29, with pre-orders open. Double-decker photo op.

xbox-business.description: Microsoft's business-side presence, entirely separate from the consumer Xbox booth in Hall 7.1. One of the largest single stands in the business area and one of the ~180 that no other exhibitor shares, which in Hall 4.2 means a meeting building rather than a stand you can walk into.
xbox-business.accessNote: A 560 m² closed structure with no co-exhibitors and nothing on show from the aisle — partner and press meetings are booked in advance through Xbox, not taken at the door.
offers: Partner and publisher meetings, by prior appointment
Press appointments — the consumer booth in Hall 7.1 is where hands-on demos live
ID@Xbox and Game Pass business conversations

nintendo-business.description: Nintendo of Europe's trade presence in Hall 4.2, distinct from the large consumer booth in Hall 9.1. Registered to the European headquarters entity rather than to a brand stand, which is the usual shape of a publisher meeting compound here.
nintendo-business.accessNote: 541 m², sole occupant, no co-exhibitors. Nintendo does not take walk-ups on the business side; the Hall 9.1 booth is the public one.
offers: Publisher and retail partner meetings by appointment

tencent-business.description: Tencent's business compound, the biggest private stand in the business halls. Its consumer-facing work is elsewhere: Level Infinite in Hall 6.1 and the Worlds of Play area in Hall 8.1, both of which have their own cards.
tencent-business.accessNote: At 702 m² this is the largest single-occupant stand in the business area — a closed meeting complex, not a show floor.
offers: Publishing, investment and partnership meetings by appointment

nvidia.description: NVIDIA's only registered stand at gamescom 2026, and it is in the business area rather than the entertainment halls — developer relations, RTX and cloud partnerships rather than a demo wall.
nvidia.accessNote: 420 m², sole occupant. NVIDIA has no consumer booth this year, so everything it is doing at the show is behind this door.
offers: Developer relations and engine partnership meetings
GeForce NOW and RTX technology briefings

pavilion-spain.description: Spain's national stand, organised around ICEX, the Spanish export agency. The single most densely shared stand in the business area: 33 studios and service companies, every one of them Spanish, listed individually in the trade list below.
pavilion-spain.accessNote: A national collective: 33 companies sharing one 240 m² stand, each with its own desk. Staffed all day and meant to be walked into — that is what a pavilion is for.
offers: 33 Spanish studios and service companies at one stand
Publishing and co-development conversations without an appointment

pavilion-malta.description: Malta's national stand, run by the Gaming Malta Foundation with the Malta Game Developers Association. Nineteen of its twenty-one exhibitors are Maltese — studios, the American University of Malta, and the agencies that sell Malta as a place to set up a studio.
pavilion-malta.accessNote: 21 exhibitors on one stand, hosted by a public foundation whose job is to be approachable. Walk up.
offers: Maltese studios and the Malta Game Developers Association
Relocation, licensing and tax advice from GamingMalta
Games education — American University of Malta

pavilion-denmark.description: Denmark's national stand, anchored by NIMBI, the country's institute for game development. Seventeen Danish studios share it, including Ghost Ship Games and Bedtime Digital Games.
pavilion-denmark.accessNote: 17 exhibitors, all Danish, on one shared stand — a collective built for walk-up conversation.
offers: NIMBI — Denmark's Institute for Game Development

pavilion-uk.description: The British collective in Hall 3.2, seventeen of its twenty-three exhibitors registered in the UK. A mix of publishers (505 Games), specialist services and PR agencies rather than a single company's compound.
pavilion-uk.accessNote: A 1,004 m² shared stand carrying 23 exhibitors — one of the two biggest collectives in the business area, and staffed throughout.
offers: 23 UK publishers, studios and service companies
Publishing and PR conversations without an appointment

pavilion-nordic.description: A joint Nordic and Baltic stand: 40 exhibitors, mostly Finnish, Norwegian, Estonian and Swedish, brought together by regional development agencies such as Business Tampere and Arctic Game Skellefteå rather than by one country's export body.
pavilion-nordic.accessNote: 40 exhibitors share this one stand — the most crowded collective in the business area. Nothing about it is closed.
offers: 40 Nordic and Baltic studios and regional agencies
Regional funding, relocation and cluster advice

games-hubs-hessen.description: The German state of Hessen's games cluster, sharing one Hall 4.1 stand with 17 other exhibitors — studios, service firms and, unusually for a games hall, the Frankfurt Book Fair.
games-hubs-hessen.accessNote: A regional cluster stand shared by 18 exhibitors, including the Frankfurter Buchmesse — open, staffed and used for introductions.
offers: Cross-media contacts — Frankfurter Buchmesse shares the stand

cloudflare-biz.description: The CDN and edge platform a large share of the industry's launch-day traffic runs through, here on the games side of the business: DDoS protection for live services, edge compute for matchmaking and telemetry, and Workers as a backend for smaller studios. A 63 m² stand in the services half of Hall 2.2 — no appointment, just a counter.
offers: DDoS protection and traffic delivery for live-service games
Workers / edge compute as a game backend
Zero Trust and internal tooling for studios

curseforge-overwolf.description: The mod-distribution side of the industry. CurseForge is the platform most PC modding communities actually publish through, and Overwolf — which owns it — builds the in-game overlay and creator-monetisation layer around it. Both are registered to the same Hall 2.2 stand, which is where studios go to talk about opening a game up to mods.
offers: CurseForge for Studios — official mod support and distribution

serverscom-biz.description: Bare-metal and hybrid hosting aimed squarely at game studios — dedicated servers for multiplayer backends, global points of presence for latency, and the kind of capacity planning a launch week needs. One of the bigger infrastructure stands in the business area.
serverscom-biz.accessNote: At 196 m² this is one of the larger service stands in Hall 2.2 — an open counter with meeting space behind it, so walk up to ask and book if you need a real conversation.
offers: Bare-metal and dedicated servers for game backends
Global low-latency hosting and capacity planning

unity-biz.description: The engine, on a stand you could miss if you blinked. Worth knowing it is there: for all the size of Unity's footprint in the industry, its gamescom presence is a single desk in the Hall 2.2 services row rather than a compound.
unity-biz.accessNote: A 12 m² desk — one of the smallest stands in the business area, and about as walk-up as a booth gets.

aws-biz.description: AWS for Games on a 45 m² stand in Hall 3.2 — game servers, GameLift, analytics pipelines and the cloud-build side of production. Smaller than you would expect for the size of the business, and in the developer hall rather than the publisher one.
offers: Analytics, data pipelines and live-ops tooling
Cloud build and CI for large projects

xsolla-biz.description: Payments, web shops and direct-to-consumer storefronts for games — the company most studios talk to when they want to sell outside a platform holder's store. One of the larger commerce stands in Hall 2.2.
xsolla-biz.accessNote: 162 m² with meeting space — Xsolla runs scheduled partner meetings at the show, but the front of the stand is staffed for walk-ups.
offers: Payments and global cash-out for game sales

keywords-biz.description: The largest games service group in the industry: art, co-development, localisation, QA, audio and player support, assembled from dozens of studios. If a game shipped in eight languages, there is a fair chance some part of it passed through here.
keywords-biz.accessNote: 122 m² with meeting space behind an open front — the co-development conversations are usually booked, the stand itself is not.
offers: Audio, voice and player support services

sumo-digital-biz.description: One of the largest independent co-development studios in Europe, with a long history of building and co-building other people's games. A work-for-hire partner rather than a publisher, which is why it stands in the services hall rather than the publisher row.
sumo-digital-biz.accessNote: 133 m² in Hall 2.1 — an open stand with meeting space; project conversations are usually pre-booked.

virtuos-biz.description: A global co-development and art-production group — remasters, ports and large-scale asset work for AAA projects. A 66 m² stand in the Hall 2.2 services row.
offers: Art production and asset pipelines at scale

denuvo-biz.description: The anti-tamper and anti-cheat company whose name turns up in more PC storefront discussions than it would probably like. A 24 m² stand in Hall 2.1 — protection, anti-cheat and mobile security, sold to studios rather than argued about with players.

ign-humble-biz.description: Two sibling businesses on one 30 m² stand: IGN, for coverage and media partnerships, and Humble Bundle, for bundle placement and charity promotions. This is the press-and-promotion end of Hall 2.1, and it is a stand you talk your way onto rather than book.
offers: Media and coverage conversations with IGN
Humble Bundle placement and charity bundles

fandom-biz.description: The wiki network that most games end up documented on whether or not anyone planned it, here as a media and advertising business. A 78 m² stand in Hall 2.1, near the rest of the games press.

reddit-biz.description: Registered as media, on one of the smallest stands in the business area. For a platform where a game's subreddit is often its most active community, the gamescom footprint is a single desk in Hall 2.2.
reddit-biz.accessNote: 16 m² — a desk, not a compound. Walk up.

opera-biz.description: The browser company, here on the strength of Opera GX — the gaming browser with a genuinely large young audience, and an advertising and partnership business attached to it. An 85 m² stand in Hall 2.2.

sensor-tower-biz.description: Market intelligence for mobile and games — the download, revenue and ad-spend estimates that turn up in half the industry's slide decks. Small stand, disproportionately consulted product.
sensor-tower-biz.accessNote: A 12 m² desk in the Hall 2.2 services row.

igda-biz.description: The International Game Developers Association, on a 45 m² stand in Hall 3.2 — with the IGDA Foundation next door at C014/D015 and Women in Games International beside them at C012/D013. Three developer-advocacy organisations in a row, which makes that corner of 3.2 the place to go for careers, community and support rather than deals.
offers: The IGDA Foundation's scholarship and support programs

wigi-biz.description: Advocacy, mentorship and hiring support for women in the games industry, on a 45 m² stand in Hall 3.2 immediately beside the IGDA and the IGDA Foundation.

owlchemy-biz.description: The VR studio behind Job Simulator and Vacation Simulator, and one of the few names in Hall 3.2 that consumers would recognise. Google-owned, and here on the developer side rather than with a demo booth.

poki-biz.description: One of the largest browser-games platforms in the world, and a real distribution route for small web-playable titles. Worth knowing it exhibits at all — it is easy to miss between the national pavilions in Hall 4.1.
poki-biz.accessNote: A 20 m² stand in Hall 4.1, among the indie and developer collectives rather than the publisher compounds.
offers: Publishing and revenue share for web games

blacknut-biz.description: A cloud-gaming subscription platform that distributes through telcos and TV operators rather than direct to players — which makes it a distribution channel most studios never think to ask about. 90 m² in Hall 3.2.

gcore-biz.description: Edge infrastructure and CDN built around game hosting — server capacity, streaming delivery and DDoS protection, sitting a few stands from Cloudflare in the same Hall 2.2 row. If you are comparing hosting at the show, they are next to each other on purpose.
offers: Game server hosting and edge delivery

hasbro-biz.description: Hasbro's business compound, shared by Hasbro Inc., Hasbro U.K. and Wizards of the Coast LLC with its two video game studios — Invoke (Warlock: Dungeons & Dragons) and Archetype (Exodus). Licensing and partner meetings for the toy, tabletop and games lines; neither video game is playable here or anywhere else on the floor.
hasbro-biz.accessNote: 196 m² held by five Hasbro entities and nobody else, registered under Entertainment and Analog Games rather than services — a meeting building, not a counter.
offers: Licensing and brand partnerships for Dungeons & Dragons and Magic: The Gathering
Publishing and co-development meetings for Invoke and Archetype
Retail and distribution appointments for the tabletop lines

kakao-games-biz.description: The Korean publisher behind Odin and the Western operation of several large Korean titles, here on a small Hall 2.2 stand for publishing and licensing conversations rather than a demo presence.
kakao-games-biz.accessNote: A 20 m² stand — small enough that it is a conversation, not a booking.
offers: Publishing and licensing for Korean and Western markets

epic-games-biz.description: Epic's business-area stand only appeared in the official directory during show week — a late Hall 4.2 registration, filed under Development, which is where Unreal Engine and the Epic Games Store sit. No booth programme is published. Epic also co-exhibits on the Hall 7.1 block shared by Webedia's FYNG City and AMD.
epic-games-biz.accessNote: 264 m² with no co-exhibitors — a closed meeting structure rather than a counter you can walk up to.
offers: Unreal Engine developer and partner meetings
Epic Games Store distribution and publishing conversations

capcom-business.description: Capcom's trade presence, registered to its German entity and a full hall away from the consumer booth in 9.1. Publisher, retail and press meetings rather than anything you can play.
capcom-business.accessNote: 276 m² with no co-exhibitors — a meeting building. The Hall 9.1 booth is where the demos are.

ubisoft-business.description: Ubisoft's German entity on a large closed stand in the publisher row of Hall 4.2, separate from its consumer booths across the grounds in 6.1. The jury named the Ubisoft Business Lounge the show's Best Business Booth.
ubisoft-business.accessNote: 403 m², sole occupant. Nothing on show from the aisle — the two Hall 6.1 stands are the public ones.

bandai-namco-business.description: One of the biggest private stands in Hall 4.2, registered to Bandai Namco's German arm. Licensing, distribution and press, with the playable side of the show in Hall 6.1.
bandai-namco-business.accessNote: 543 m² and no co-exhibitors — the third-largest single stand in the business area, and entirely closed.

sega-business.description: SEGA Europe's meeting side of the show: a closed stand in Hall 2.1, halfway across the grounds from the Hall 7.1 booth where its games are playable. Licensing, distribution and partner talks.
sega-business.accessNote: 446 m² and closed. The two stands next to it — E054 and C050/E051, another 830 m² — are filed to The Junction / SEGA, so the whole corner is one appointment-only compound.

snail-games-business.description: The ARK publisher's trade-side table in Hall 3.2, added to its show alongside the Hall 8.1 consumer booth. Publishing, licensing and platform talks.
snail-games-business.accessNote: 15 m² with a single occupant — a table booth you can walk up to, not a meeting room.

cdpr-business.description: CD Projekt S.A. — the group above CD Projekt Red and GOG — on a large closed stand in Hall 4.2. Partner and press meetings; the consumer booth is in Hall 8.1.
cdpr-business.accessNote: 432 m², sole occupant, filed to the parent company rather than to CD Projekt Red or GOG. CD Projekt Red's guided Songs of the Past presentations run here Aug 26–28 only, by appointment.

krafton-business.description: KRAFTON's trade stand, separate from the two consumer booths it runs in Hall 9.1. Publishing, investment and partnership conversations.
krafton-business.accessNote: 245 m², sole occupant — a closed stand in the Hall 4.2 publisher row.

atari-business.description: Atari on the business side: licensing its back catalogue, the hardware partnerships behind the recent re-releases, and publishing. The retro-facing consumer booth is in Hall 10.1.
atari-business.accessNote: 162 m² in the publisher row — mid-sized rather than a compound, so expect a staffed front with meeting space behind it.

giants-software-business.description: The Farming Simulator studio and publisher on the trade side, where the licensing deals that put real agricultural brands into the game get done. The playable booth is in Hall 6.1.
giants-software-business.accessNote: 178 m², sole occupant — a working stand rather than a closed compound, but the meetings are booked.

hoyoverse-business.description: HoYoverse's trade stand, registered to its Singapore entity and filed under merchandising as well as games — which is most of what the business side is for. The consumer booth is in Hall 6.1.
hoyoverse-business.accessNote: 104 m² — small for Hall 4.2, so a staffed stand rather than a sealed building, but meetings are arranged in advance.

focus-business.description: The French publisher's trade stand, where it signs and shows work to partners rather than players.
focus-business.accessNote: 210 m², sole occupant — a closed stand. Focus's playable line-up is in Hall 6.1.

aerosoft-business.description: The simulation publisher and distributor on the trade side — flight and train sim licensing, and the boxed-retail distribution business that is easy to forget still exists. Consumer booth in Hall 9.1.
aerosoft-business.accessNote: 93 m² — one of the smaller stands in Hall 4.2 and an open one.

level-infinite-business.description: Tencent's publishing label, registered as Proxima Beta and sharing one of the few large *shared* stands in Hall 4.2 rather than a compound of its own. Its consumer booth is in Hall 6.1; the separate 702 m² Tencent Technology stand nearby is closed.
level-infinite-business.accessNote: A 512 m² stand shared with six other publishers — Bohemia Interactive, Digital Extremes, Funcom, Paradox, Remedy and Techland. Shared means staffed and walkable, unlike the sealed compounds around it.
offers: Six other publishers on the same stand

ncsoft-business.description: The Korean publisher behind Lineage, Guild Wars 2 and Throne and Liberty, running business-only meetings in Hall 4.2 — no consumer showcase this year.
ncsoft-business.accessNote: A 306 m² single-occupant stand — closed, appointment-only.

raw-fury-business.description: The Swedish indie publisher, on the business side where submissions and signings happen. Its games are playable in the indie half of Hall 10.1.
raw-fury-business.accessNote: 116 m² in Hall 2.1 — a working stand with meeting space, and the place indies actually pitch them.

coffee-stain-business.description: Coffee Stain Publishing on the trade side: the label behind Satisfactory and Deep Rock Galactic taking submissions. The consumer booth is in Hall 10.1.
coffee-stain-business.accessNote: 110 m² in Hall 2.1 — a staffed stand where the meetings are booked but the front is not.

razer-business.description: Razer's European entity on the trade side — retail, distribution and the developer programs behind Chroma and its haptics. The consumer hardware booth is in Hall 10.2.
razer-business.accessNote: On a 576 m² stand shared with fourteen other exhibitors, so it is an open counter rather than a private booth.

corsair-business.description: Corsair on the trade side, filed under components and accessories: retail, distribution and the Elgato side of the business. The product wall is in Hall 10.1.
corsair-business.accessNote: 74 m² and open — the components-and-accessories row of Hall 2.2 is a retail floor, not a meeting corridor.

samsung-business.description: Samsung Electronics on the trade side, filed under platforms and components — displays, panels and the retail relationships behind them, rather than the Odyssey monitors you can sit at in Hall 9.1.
samsung-business.accessNote: 36 m² — a small open stand, nothing like the Odyssey booth in Hall 9.1.

bloober-team-business.description: The Polish horror studio on the business side, taking co-development and publishing meetings. Its games are playable in Hall 10.1.
bloober-team-business.accessNote: 72 m² and open — a working stand in the Hall 2.2 services row.

wargaming-business.description: Wargaming's only registered stand at the show, on the trade side in Hall 2.2. Worth knowing, because the guide otherwise lists them as having no show-floor presence at all.
wargaming-business.accessNote: 20 m² — a desk. Wargaming has no consumer booth on the show floor this year, so this is its whole gamescom presence.

scs-software-business.description: The Euro Truck Simulator studio, here on its country's shared stand rather than a booth of its own. Licensing — real truck brands and cargo liveries — is most of what the trade side is for. The playable booth is in Hall 10.1.
scs-software-business.accessNote: On the Czech collective stand in Hall 4.1, shared with thirteen other exhibitors — open and staffed.
offers: Thirteen other Czech studios on the same stand

area-35-business.description: The publisher on its trade stand, taking submissions and distribution meetings. Its games are playable in Hall 10.1.
area-35-business.accessNote: 61 m², open — a stand you can walk up to in the Hall 2.2 row.

4divinity.description: GCL's publishing arm, showing six titles across three stands: the main one in Hall 7.1, an outpost in Hall 6.1 and a business booth in Hall 4.2. Three are hands-on — The Defiant and Guns of Eschaton at the Hall 7.1 stand, Showa American Story at the 6.1 outpost — while the rest show as trailers.
4divinity.crowdNote: A large Hall 7.1 stand beside Xbox, but a lineup still new to Western audiences — busy without AAA-scale queues.
4divinity.visitAdvice: The two stands show different games: Showa American Story and The Defiant in Hall 6.1, Guns of Eschaton in Hall 7.1. Check which one you actually want before walking over.

games.The Defiant: 15-minute hands-on demo at the Hall 7.1 B021 stand — the WWII shooter's first playable in the West.
games.Showa American Story: Hands-on demo at the Hall 6.1 outpost (stand A030) — NEKCOM's retro pop-culture RPG, due 2026.
games.Guns of Eschaton: Playable at the main Hall 7.1 stand — and a Best PC Game nominee at the gamescom award.
games.A Whisper of Fall: Jinyiwei: Ming-dynasty action RPG from CangMo Game Entertainment — showcase presence, no demo station reported.
games.Genigods: Nezha: The hands-on runs at the platform booths — play it at Xbox's Hall 7.1 stand; shown as part of the showcase here.
games.Sword Sage: Awakening: Myth-driven action RPG from Sword Panda — showcase presence, no demo station reported.

secret-mode.description: Sumo Group's publishing label takes a Hall 6.1 stand at B040, and its one game is playable: STAR WARS: Galactic Racer, run as time-trial races with a daily fastest-lap prize.
secret-mode.crowdNote: A small stand for an indie-scale publisher — walk-up.
secret-mode.visitAdvice: A Star Wars racer on a small stand could draw more than the stand can absorb. Nothing hands-on is announced yet, so look before you commit to a queue.

games.STAR WARS: Galactic Racer: Playable — time-trial races with a prize for the fastest daily time. Fuse Games (Burnout veterans); out October 2026.

pawprint-aniimo.description: Singapore's Pawprint Interactive at Hall 6.1 C041, registered under its game's own brand: Aniimo, an open-world creature-collecting RPG for PC, console and mobile.
pawprint-aniimo.crowdNote: Creature-collectors draw steady interest and this is a mid-size stand — expect a short rotating line.
pawprint-aniimo.visitAdvice: Sits in the same Hall 6.1 aisle as Elementa Games and Secret Mode, so the three make one short detour off the publisher row.

games.Aniimo: Playable on GeForce RTX demo stations — and the launch dates landed at the show: Sept 16 on PC and consoles, Sept 23 on mobile.

elementa-games.description: Singapore developer Elementa, with a Hall 6.1 stand at C021 and a business booth in Hall 2.2. Silver Palace is playable in a demo area with four daily stage shows, photo spots and merch — the PS5 version and 'House of Greed' multiplayer were revealed at the show.
elementa-games.crowdNote: Small stand with an all-but-unannounced lineup — low queues.
elementa-games.visitAdvice: A discovery stop rather than a planned one.

games.Silver Palace: Playable demo area plus four daily stage shows — PS5 version and 'House of Greed' multiplayer revealed at the show; a gamescom award Best Mobile Game nominee.

huawei-appgallery.description: Aspiegel SE — Huawei's European entity — running AppGallery and its GameCenter at Hall 7.1 B031. A mobile-platform stand rather than a games booth: it is filed under app stores, platforms and mobile phones.
huawei-appgallery.crowdNote: Platform stand: browse-through, no demo queues.
huawei-appgallery.visitAdvice: A two-minute stop between Xbox and Konami if mobile storefronts are of interest.

webedia-fyng-city.description: FYNG City, the games-media village Webedia builds in Hall 7.1: over 1,500 m² across three stands — B051/C050, B041/C040 and C052 — with the GameStar and MeinMMO editorial teams on site and Mercedes-Benz as main partner. Webedia's registered brands here include GameStar, GamePro, MeinMMO, Moviepilot and Filmstarts.
webedia-fyng-city.crowdNote: A hangout area rather than a demo queue — busy but flowing.
webedia-fyng-city.visitAdvice: One of the few places in Hall 7 to sit down mid-hall. AMD's stand shares the same block at B041/C040, and Epic Games registered there too, as a co-exhibitor filing under Unreal Engine.

mbc-game-studio.description: A large Hall 8.1 stand — roughly 610 m² at A011/B010, at the far end of the hall next to Square Enix — plus a business booth in Hall 2.1, for the British-Saudi studio, registered under the brand 'MGS'. Its debut game arrived with ONL: 1001: Threads of Mizan, playable on the stand.
mbc-game-studio.crowdNote: The booth size implies a real presence, but with no announced lineup the draw is unknown.
mbc-game-studio.visitAdvice: Worth a look on your first pass down Hall 8.1 — it is one of the hall's bigger unknowns.

games.1001: Threads of Mizan: MBC's debut, revealed at ONL with a playable demo on the show floor — three-player co-op action rooted in Arabic folklore, from a team with Fortnite veterans. No release window yet.

mbc-game-studio-business.description: MBC Game Studio's business-hall stand, separate from its large Hall 8.1 showcase. Publishing and partnership meetings for the British-Saudi studio.
mbc-game-studio-business.accessNote: A single-code stand in Hall 2.1, filed under the studio alone rather than a shared pavilion.

the-district.description: New for 2026: a competitive-gaming area of about 2,000 m² in Hall 8.1 plus roughly 1,000 m² in the reactivated outdoor area P8 behind the hall, with an esports stage at the back of the hall. Cologne's SK Gaming is the headline partner; REWE, Techniker Krankenkasse, Nestlé, Logitech, Deutsche Telekom, Philips, SanDisk, Subway and Esports Virtual Arenas are among the brands on the shared stand and around it.
the-district.crowdNote: Stage-driven: quiet between sessions, packed while a tournament runs.
the-district.visitAdvice: Come for a scheduled session rather than wandering in. The P8 outdoor half is straight out the back of Hall 8 and also holds CD Projekt Red's Apollo Tent, the Red Bull bar and the gamescom Beach.

games.Clutch: Maverick Games' open-world driving game, hands-on all five days in the P8 outdoor half.
games.Star Wars Galactic Racer: A pre-show trade-press line placed it at HP/HyperX in the P8 outdoor half, but day-1 sources don't corroborate it — the game's official gamescom page names only Secret Mode's Hall 6.1 stand, the sure place to play it.
games.EA Sports FC 27: Red Bull runs an FC 27 tournament at its booth in the P8 outdoor area — separate from EA's own Hall 6.1 stand.

gigabyte-aorus.description: GIGABYTE and its AORUS gaming brand at Hall 8.1 C050: graphics cards, monitors, laptops and peripherals, registered across components, displays and VR.
gigabyte-aorus.visitAdvice: Part of the same Hall 8.1 hardware run as ASUS ROG, AGON by AOC and Logitech.

mattel.description: Mattel's first gamescom with a stand of its own, and it has two: Hall 8.1 B020 in the hall entrance area beside CD Projekt Red and Square Enix, with six playable Mattel Game Studios titles, the Mattel Brick Shop sets (including a 3,500-piece Xbox console), a live stage and Minecraft and KPop Demon Hunters photo spots, with Barbie Rewind added to its booth page since — plus the Mattel Fan Shop at Hall 5.1 C024 in the Merchandise Area, which is where the buying happens.
mattel.crowdNote: Family-facing brand stand; the demos are short mobile sessions, so waits stay small except at the weekend and around stage slots.
mattel.visitAdvice: The Hall 8.1 stand is a quick stop on the way in or out of Hall 8 — five of its six demos are mobile and turn over fast. If you came to buy the Brick Shop sets rather than play, go to the Hall 5.1 fan shop instead; only it sells.

games.He-Man and the Masters of the Universe:: The one PC/console title on the stand — Bitmap Bureau's retro brawler, out since April.
games.Skeletor: Until Next Time!: Mattel Game Studios' first self-published game, an endless runner already on iOS and Android.
games.Barbie Rewind: Presented on the day-1 booth stage ('Play Through the Decades', with Digital Eclipse) — a live look, not a demo station; launches Nov 12.

jbl-quantum.description: Harman's JBL and JBL Quantum gaming-audio line at Hall 9.1 B034/C035 — headsets, headphones and speakers to try on.
jbl-quantum.crowdNote: Small listening stand, no real queue.
jbl-quantum.visitAdvice: Two minutes off the Nintendo-to-Capcom walk through Hall 9.1.

rocket-beans.description: Rocket Beans TV broadcasts the whole show from Hall 9.1 A046/B047 — filed under BEANS Entertainment GmbH — and runs a second stage at the Capcom stand daily from 11:30, including the new BEANSCOMPETITION at 17:00. Live from Tuesday evening through Sunday, with a separate merch stand in Hall 5.2.
rocket-beans.crowdNote: German-language streaming audience: crowds gather for the scheduled formats and thin out between them.
rocket-beans.visitAdvice: Come for a specific slot. The Capcom-stand programme covers Onimusha: Way of the Sword, Dragon's Dogma 2, Mega Man: Dual Override, Street Fighter 6 and Pragmata.

gamescom-merch.description: The official gamescom merchandise shops, run by Campus Sportswear under the gamescomwear brand. The main shops are in the Hall 5.2 merchandise area, with smaller counters in Halls 6.1, 7.1, 8.1, 9.1, 10.1 and 10.2 — which is what those unnamed kiosks along the entertainment-hall aisles are.
gamescom-merch.crowdNote: The Hall 5.2 shops build queues; the in-hall counters stay short.
gamescom-merch.visitAdvice: Use whichever counter is in the hall you are already in rather than walking to Hall 5.2 for it.

gateron.description: Mechanical keyboard switches from the brand behind most third-party switch sets on the market, registered under its legal entity Huizhou Jiadalong Electronic Technology — one of Hall 10.1's less obvious hardware-row stands.
gateron.crowdNote: A quiet component stand, not a destination booth.
gateron.visitAdvice: A quick look if you're already working the hardware row.

deepcool.description: PC cooling and case hardware on display in Hall 10.1's hardware row — coolers, fans and cases from the 2026 line.
deepcool.crowdNote: Steady component-shopper traffic, no real queue.
deepcool.visitAdvice: Any time; pair with the rest of the hardware row.

lexar.description: Flash memory and SD/microSD cards in Hall 10.1's hardware row — storage for Switch 2, Steam Deck and handheld PCs.
lexar.crowdNote: A quiet component stand, not a destination booth.
lexar.visitAdvice: A quick look if you're already working the hardware row.

xppen.description: Drawing tablets and pen displays from the brand, registered under its legal entity Hanvon Ugee Technology — aimed at the show's digital-art and streaming crowd.
xppen.crowdNote: A quiet component stand, not a destination booth.
xppen.visitAdvice: A quick look if you're already working the hardware row.

epomaker.description: Mechanical keyboards from the brand's 2026 line, on display in Hall 10.1's hardware row.
epomaker.crowdNote: Steady hobbyist traffic, no real queue.
epomaker.visitAdvice: Any time; pair with the rest of the hardware row.

iqunix.description: Mechanical keyboards from the brand's 2026 line, on display in Hall 10.1's hardware row.
iqunix.crowdNote: A quiet component stand, not a destination booth.
iqunix.visitAdvice: A quick look if you're already working the hardware row.

genki.description: Handheld gaming accessories — docks, cases and controllers — from the brand, registered under its legal entity Human Things.
genki.crowdNote: A quiet component stand, not a destination booth.
genki.visitAdvice: A quick look if you're already working the hardware row.

havit.description: Budget peripherals — keyboards, mice, headsets — from the brand, registered under its legal entity Guangzhou Havit Technology.
havit.crowdNote: A quiet component stand, not a destination booth.
havit.visitAdvice: A quick look if you're already working the hardware row.

karnox.description: Gaming and racing-sim chairs from the brand's 2026 line, on display in Hall 10.1's hardware row.
karnox.crowdNote: A quiet component stand, not a destination booth.
karnox.visitAdvice: A quick look if you're already working the hardware row.

diablo-chairs.description: Gaming chairs from the European brand, registered under its legal entity Domator24 — shares a stand with iiyama.
diablo-chairs.crowdNote: A quiet component stand, not a destination booth.
diablo-chairs.visitAdvice: A quick look if you're already working the hardware row.

iiyama.description: Gaming monitors from the established display brand — shares a stand with Diablo Chairs in Hall 10.1's hardware row.
iiyama.crowdNote: A quiet component stand, not a destination booth.
iiyama.visitAdvice: A quick look if you're already working the hardware row.

retro-area.description: The exhibition half of the Retro & Family Area: about 2,000 m² across seven Hall 10.2 stands, put together by René Meyer's Haus der Computerspiele with around 50 collectors, clubs and institutions, Berlin's Computerspielemuseum among them. Working consoles, arcade cabinets and home computers from five decades — Pong, the 80s arcades, C64 and Amiga, Super Nintendo — most of them there to be played, plus pinball, dance cabinets and a stage.
retro-area.crowdNote: Hundreds of machines over a lot of floor, so it absorbs a crowd — but the headline cabinets and the stage seats fill up at the weekend.
retro-area.visitAdvice: Nothing here has a queue worth planning around, so treat it as browsing time — an hour goes quickly. Check the stage schedule first: the German Classic Tetris Championship is played on it, alongside quizzes, interviews and live music, with Commodore's Petro Tyschtschenko and composers Chris Hülsbeck and David Wise among the guests. The world's largest Pac-Man cabinet and a Vectrex Mini prototype are what people come to photograph. The separate collectors' stand at A020 next door is worth the extra few minutes.

retro-games.description: Officially licensed retro-console recreations — THEC64 Mini, TheA500 Mini and similar — from the UK brand behind them, in Hall 10.2's retro corner.
retro-games.crowdNote: Nostalgia traffic from visitors who grew up on the originals; browsable, not a queue.
retro-games.visitAdvice: Combine with the rest of Hall 10.2's retro and family area.

ravensburger.description: The German board-game and puzzle publisher's stand in Hall 5.2's Cards & Boards Area — new releases and demo tables.
ravensburger.crowdNote: Family and hobbyist traffic; busiest around scheduled demo slots.
ravensburger.visitAdvice: Any afternoon works; go early for a seat at a demo table.

panini.description: Stickers and trading cards from the global collectibles publisher, in Hall 5.2's Cards & Boards Area.
panini.crowdNote: Steady collector traffic, busier around new set releases.
panini.visitAdvice: Any time; pair with the rest of Hall 5.2's card and collectible stands.

bushiroad.description: Cardfight!! Vanguard and Weiss Schwarz publisher's stand in Hall 5.2's Cards & Boards Area — tournaments and demo tables for its TCG lineup.
bushiroad.crowdNote: Dedicated TCG crowd; busiest during scheduled tournament slots.
bushiroad.visitAdvice: Check the stand's own schedule for tournament times if you want to play.

pegasus-spiele.description: The German board-game publisher and distributor's stand in Hall 5.2's Cards & Boards Area — new releases and demo tables.
pegasus-spiele.crowdNote: Family and hobbyist traffic; busiest around scheduled demo slots.
pegasus-spiele.visitAdvice: Any afternoon works; go early for a seat at a demo table.

purearts.description: Licensed video-game statues and collectibles from the Canadian maker, in Hall 5.2's Cards & Boards Area.
purearts.crowdNote: Browsable collector traffic, no real queue.
purearts.visitAdvice: Any time; pair with the rest of Hall 5.2's collectible stands.

tsume-art.description: Collectible statues from the Luxembourg-based maker, in Hall 5.1.
tsume-art.crowdNote: Browsable collector traffic, no real queue.

fangamer.description: Officially licensed indie-game merchandise — Undertale, Stardew Valley and similar — from the well-known online shop, in Hall 5.1.
fangamer.crowdNote: Steady fan traffic for new drops; browsable otherwise.
fangamer.visitAdvice: Go early on the first public day for limited-run items.

game-informer.description: The relaunched games-media outlet's booth in Hall 10.1, covering the show floor.
game-informer.crowdNote: A media stand, not a destination booth.
game-informer.visitAdvice: A quick look if you're already in the area.

shueisha-games.description: The games arm of manga publisher Shueisha (Shonen Jump), on a shared Hall 10.2 stand block — a six-title lineup with five hands-on, headlined by the first public reveal of the 5X strategy game Conquista. The Jujutsu Kaisen game its booth page once registered isn't at the show; its playable debut is Tokyo Game Show.
shueisha-games.crowdNote: A browsing stand in the indie half of Hall 10.2 — short waits, if any.
shueisha-games.visitAdvice: Worth a pass if you follow Shonen Jump. It sits a few stands from the Indie Arena Booth, so fold it into that walk.

games.BAKUDO: New playable demo — boss-rush action with competitive ball-sport mechanics, by SAYIL Games.
games.Chronoscript: The Endless End: New playable demo — exploration action-adventure where you play an editor inside a broken manuscript.
games.UN:Me: Playable build plus a new gameplay trailer — a psychological adventure about a girl carrying multiple souls; PS5, Switch 2 and Steam in 2026.
games.Schrödinger's Call: In the six-title lineup, the only one without a demo call-out — the end-of-the-world visual novel released in May.
games.Wild Wild Eden: First public hands-on demo — open-world survival-crafting in a primitive fantasy setting; Steam Early Access spring 2027.
games.Conquista: First public reveal, with a hands-on demo — a 5X strategy game of conquest, expansion and colony management by Microsimulation.

metanet.description: The Canadian studio behind the ninja platformers N and N++ brings one title to its small Hall 10.2 stand: N PLUS INFINITY TIMES TWO, named on its gamescom booth page. Hands-on is not announced.
metanet.crowdNote: A one-game stand in the indie half of the hall — little to no wait.
metanet.visitAdvice: A two-minute stop on the way through Hall 10.2; the Indie Arena Booth is a few stands over.

games.N PLUS INFINITY TIMES TWO: The N++ follow-up, named on Metanet's gamescom booth page; no hands-on announced.
